title.en: Volume 309 Biographies 68: Wang Yande, Chang Yanxin, Cheng Dexuan, Wang Yande, Wei Zhen, Zhang Zhi, Yang Yungong, Qin Xi, Xie Dequan, Yan Rixin, Jin Huaide
title.raw: 卷三百〇九 列傳第六十八 王延德 常延信 程德玄 王延德 魏震 張質 楊允恭 秦羲 謝德權 閻日新 靳懷德 Volume 309 Biographies 68: Wang Yande, Chang Yanxin, Cheng Dexuan, Wang Yande, Wei Zhen, Zhang Zhi, Yang Yungong, Qin Xi, Xie Dequan, Yan Rixin, Jin Huaide

sentences.zh: 王延德

translations.literal: Wang Yande
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yande

sentences.zh: 王延德，開封東明人。

translations.literal: Wang Yande was a native of Dongming in Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yande was from Dongming in Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 曾祖芝，濮陽令。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Zhi was magistrate of Puyang.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Zhi served as magistrate of Puyang.

sentences.zh: 祖璋，相州錄事參軍。

translations.literal: His grandfather Zhang was recording secretary of Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Zhang held the post of recording secretary in Xiang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 父溫，晉末契丹內寇，溫率鄉豪捍蔽境內，里人德之。

translations.literal: His father Wen, at the end of Jin when the Khitans raided within the borders, Wen led local notables to defend the territory, and the people of the district were grateful to him.
translations.idiomatic: His father Wen, when the Khitans invaded late in the Jin period, led local leaders in defending the region, earning the gratitude of the community.

sentences.zh: 宣祖掌畿甸兵，與溫厚善，延德方總角，宣祖愛其謹重，召置左右。

translations.literal: The founding emperor commanded the capital-region forces and was on close terms with Wen; Yande was still a boy, and the founding emperor admired his prudence and steadiness and summoned him to attend at his side.
translations.idiomatic: While the founding emperor held command of the capital armies, he was on warm terms with Wen. Yande was still a child, and the founding emperor, taken with his careful and steady manner, had him brought into his personal service.

sentences.zh: 太宗尹京，署為親校，專主庖膳，尤被倚信。

translations.literal: When Emperor Taizong governed the capital, he appointed him a personal attendant, put him in charge of the kitchens exclusively, and relied on him especially.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taizong served as governor of the capital, he appointed Yande a personal attendant in charge of the kitchens and placed exceptional trust in him.

sentences.zh: 太平興國初，授御廚副使，數月，遷正使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Taiping Xingguo era he was appointed deputy commissioner of the imperial kitchen; within a few months he was promoted to commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Taiping Xingguo reign he was made deputy commissioner of the imperial kitchen, and a few months later was promoted to commissioner.

sentences.zh: 從征太原，未幾，加尚食使，賜浚儀縣壽昌坊宅一區。

translations.literal: He followed the campaign against Taiyuan; before long he was given the additional title of commissioner of imperial provisions and granted one residence in Shouchang Ward, Junyi County.
translations.idiomatic: He accompanied the expedition against Taiyuan and soon afterward was made commissioner of imperial provisions and granted a house in Shouchang Ward of Junyi County.

sentences.zh: 俄領薊州刺史，兼掌武德司，改皇城使，掌御輦院、左藏庫。

translations.literal: Shortly he also held the prefecture of Jizhou, concurrently directed the Wude Bureau, was changed to commissioner of the imperial city, and managed the imperial carriage park and the left treasury.
translations.idiomatic: He soon took charge of Jizhou as prefect while also directing the Wude Bureau, then became commissioner of the imperial city with authority over the imperial carriage park and the left treasury.

sentences.zh: 延德所領凡五印，因對懇讓，遂罷左藏、御廚。

translations.literal: Yande altogether held five seals of office; on an audience he earnestly declined, and the left treasury and imperial kitchen were then removed from his charge.
translations.idiomatic: Yande held as many as five official seals at once; when he appeared in audience and earnestly declined the burden, he was relieved of the left treasury and the imperial kitchen.

sentences.zh: 八年，兼充親王諸宮使。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was also made commissioner of the princes' palaces.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was additionally appointed commissioner of the princes' palaces.

sentences.zh: 延德素謹慎，以舊恩，每延訪外事。

translations.literal: Yande had always been cautious; because of his old favor, the emperor would often summon him to inquire about outside affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Yande was by nature cautious, and on account of their long-standing bond the emperor would often call him in to ask about affairs beyond the palace.

sentences.zh: 端拱初，領本州團練使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Duangong era he held the regimental commander of his home prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Duangong reign he was made regimental commander of his home prefecture.

sentences.zh: 淳化中，當進秩，延德與王繼恩、杜彥鈞使額已極，特置昭宣使，以延德等為之。

translations.literal: In the Chunhua era, when he was due for advancement, Yande together with Wang Jien and Du Yanjun had already reached the limit of commissioner titles, so the office of Zhaoxuan commissioner was specially created and Yande and the others were appointed to it.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chunhua period, when promotion was due, Yande, Wang Jien, and Du Yanjun had already topped out in commissioner ranks, so a new post of Zhaoxuan commissioner was created and they were appointed to it.

sentences.zh: 至道二年，加領平州防禦使。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhidao he was additionally given the defense commissioner of Pingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhidao he was also made defense commissioner of Ping Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 真宗嗣位，改領懷州。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhenzong succeeded to the throne, he was changed to hold Huaizhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhenzong came to the throne, Yande was reassigned to hold Huai Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 永熙復土，提點緣路供頓。

translations.literal: For the Yongxi tomb restoration he was made overseer of supplies along the route.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yongxi tomb restoration he was put in charge of provisioning along the route.

sentences.zh: 咸平初，出知華州，占謝日，面請罷昭宣使，從之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xianping he went out as prefect of Huazhou; on the day he took leave to give thanks, he asked in person to be relieved of the Zhaoxuan commission, and it was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Xianping he was sent out as prefect of Hua. On the day he presented his thanks for the appointment, he asked in person to be relieved of the Zhaoxuan commission, and the emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 實以禦侮正秩，奉給優厚故也。

translations.literal: In truth it was because the regular rank for repelling insult had generous salary and allowances.
translations.idiomatic: This was in fact because the regular military rank carried generous pay and perquisites.

sentences.zh: 上幸大名，為東京舊城都巡檢使。

translations.literal: When the emperor visited Daming, he served as metropolitan patrol commissioner of the old Eastern Capital city.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor traveled to Daming, Yande served as metropolitan patrol commissioner of the old Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 明年，以風痹請告，遣還本郡，是冬卒，年六十四。

translations.literal: The next year, on grounds of wind paralysis he requested leave and was sent back to his home commandery; that winter he died, aged sixty-four.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he asked for leave on account of wind paralysis and was sent home to his native prefecture, where he died that winter at the age of sixty-four.

sentences.zh: 贈邕州觀察使。

translations.literal: He was posthumously given the title of observation commissioner of Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously enfeoffed as observation commissioner of Yong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 延德所至，好撰集近事。

translations.literal: Wherever Yande served, he liked to compile collections of recent events.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever he served, Yande liked to compile records of recent events.

sentences.zh: 掌禦廚則為《司膳錄》，掌皇城司則為《皇城紀事錄》，從郊祀為行宮使則為《南郊錄》，奉詔修內則為《版築記》，從靈駕則為《永熙皇堂錄》、《山陵提轄諸司記》，及治郡則為《下車奏報錄》。

translations.literal: When he managed the imperial kitchen he wrote the 《Record of the Provisioners》; when he managed the imperial city bureau he wrote the 《Record of the Imperial City》; when he followed the suburban sacrifice as palace commissioner he wrote the 《Record of the Southern Suburb》; when he received orders to repair the inner quarters he wrote the 《Record of Construction》; when he followed the imperial coffin he wrote the 《Record of the Yongxi Imperial Hall》 and the 《Record of the Various Offices Overseeing the Imperial Tomb》, and when he governed a prefecture he wrote the 《Record of Reports upon Taking Office》.
translations.idiomatic: While in charge of the imperial kitchen he compiled the 《Record of the Provisioners》; while directing the imperial city bureau, the 《Annals of the Imperial City》; as palace commissioner on the suburban sacrifice, the 《Record of the Southern Suburb》; on imperial orders to repair the inner palace, the 《Record of Construction》; on the funeral train, the 《Record of the Yongxi Imperial Hall》 and the 《Record of the Tomb Offices》; and as prefect, the 《Record of Reports upon Taking Office》.

sentences.zh: 先是，詔史官修太祖、太宗《實錄》，多以國初事訪延德，又上《太宗南宮事跡》三卷。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the court historians were ordered to compile the 《Veritable Records》 of Taizu and Taizong, they often consulted Yande about events of the founding era, and he also presented three fascicles of the 《Taizong's Affairs in the Southern Palace》.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when court historians were ordered to compile the 《Veritable Records》 of Taizu and Taizong, they frequently consulted Yande about the founding period, and he also submitted three fascicles of the 《Taizong's Affairs in the Southern Palace》.

sentences.zh: 子：應昌，莊宅使、端州團練使。

translations.literal: Son: Yingchang, commissioner of the crown estates and regimental commander of Duanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yingchang served as commissioner of the crown estates and regimental commander of Duan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 常延信

translations.literal: Chang Yanxin
translations.idiomatic: Chang Yanxin

sentences.zh: 常延信，幷州平晉人。

translations.literal: Chang Yanxin was a native of Pingjin in Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Chang Yanxin was from Pingjin in Bing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 祖思，仕周歷昭義、歸德、平盧三鎮節度，延信皆補牙職，領和州刺史。

translations.literal: His grandfather Si, serving Zhou, successively held the military governorships of Zhaoyi, Guide, and Pinglu; Yanxin was repeatedly appointed to staff posts in his yamen and held the prefecture of Hezhou.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Si, while serving the Zhou, held in turn the governorships of Zhaoyi, Guide, and Pinglu; Yanxin served repeatedly on his staff and was made prefect of He Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 思卒，入為六宅使，領郡如故。

translations.literal: When Si died, he entered the capital as commissioner of the six residences while continuing to hold the prefecture as before.
translations.idiomatic: After Si's death he was summoned to the capital as commissioner of the six residences while retaining his prefectural post.

sentences.zh: 建隆初，改領平州，坐與妻族相訟，左授右監門衛副率，領護滑州黃河堤。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianlong he was changed to hold Pingzhou; because he was involved in litigation with his wife's kin he was demoted to deputy commandant of the right Gate Guard and put in charge of the Yellow River dikes at Huazhou.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Jianlong he was reassigned to Ping Prefecture, but after a lawsuit with his wife's family he was demoted to deputy commandant of the Right Gate Guard and assigned to maintain the Yellow River dikes at Hua Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 開寶中，為京新城外汴河南巡檢，出為潼關監軍。

translations.literal: In the Kaibao era he was southern patrol commissioner along the Bian River outside the new capital city; he then went out as military supervisor of Tong Pass.
translations.idiomatic: During the Kaibao period he patrolled the Bian River south of the new capital, then was sent out as military supervisor of Tong Pass.

sentences.zh: 延信以關路岩險，奏易道路及填禁坑，役工四十餘萬。

translations.literal: Yanxin, because the pass road was steep and perilous, memorialized to change the route and fill in forbidden pits, employing more than four hundred thousand laborers.
translations.idiomatic: Finding the pass road steep and dangerous, Yanxin memorialized to reroute it and fill in hazardous pits, putting more than four hundred thousand laborers to work.

sentences.zh: 又監通許鎮兵，改梓、遂十二州都巡檢使，賜袍帶、錢百萬。

translations.literal: He also supervised the troops at Tongxu garrison, was changed to metropolitan patrol commissioner of the twelve prefectures of Zi and Su, and was granted robes, belt, and a million in cash.
translations.idiomatic: He next supervised the garrison at Tongxu, then became metropolitan patrol commissioner for the twelve prefectures of Zi and Su, and was granted court robes, a belt, and a million in cash.

sentences.zh: 太平興國初，秩滿，留再任，賜錢四十萬。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taiping Xingguo, when his term expired, he was kept for another appointment and given four hundred thousand in cash.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Taiping Xingguo, when his term ended, he was retained for another tour and given four hundred thousand in cash.

sentences.zh: 時亡命卒多以山林為寇，延信嘗領徒捕殺三百餘人。

translations.literal: At the time many deserters took to the mountains and forests as bandits; Yanxin once led troops in pursuit and killed more than three hundred.
translations.idiomatic: At that time many deserters turned bandit in the hills; Yanxin once led a force that killed more than three hundred of them.

sentences.zh: 又為唐、鄧都巡檢使，代還，繼改右清道、右司禦二副率。

translations.literal: He next served as metropolitan patrol commissioner of Tang and Deng; when relieved and returned, he was successively changed to deputy commandant of the right Qingdao and right Siyu guards.
translations.idiomatic: He next served as metropolitan patrol commissioner of Tang and Deng, and on returning from that post was made deputy commandant of the Right Qingdao and Right Siyu guards in succession.

sentences.zh: 雍熙三年，命督鎮州以北至軍前芻糧。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yongxi he was ordered to oversee fodder and grain from north of Zhenzhou to the front.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Yongxi he was ordered to supervise fodder and grain from north of Zhen Prefecture to the army front.

sentences.zh: 是冬，為全、邵六州都巡檢使，令疾置之任。

translations.literal: That winter he was made metropolitan patrol commissioner of the six prefectures of Quan and Shao and ordered to take up the post with dispatch.
translations.idiomatic: That winter he was made metropolitan patrol commissioner of the six prefectures of Quan and Shao and told to reach his post at once.

sentences.zh: 就充羊狀六砦都鈐轄，遷右衛副率。

translations.literal: He was then made overall commander of the six stockades at Yangzhuang and promoted to deputy commandant of the right Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was then appointed overall commander of the six stockades at Yangzhuang and promoted to deputy commandant of the Right Guard.

sentences.zh: 會誠州蠻歸款，命延信馳入溪洞，索其要領。

translations.literal: When the barbarians of Chengzhou submitted, Yanxin was ordered to ride swiftly into the stream gorges and obtain their key points.
translations.idiomatic: When the tribes of Cheng Prefecture submitted, Yanxin was ordered to ride into the gorges and secure their strategic points.

sentences.zh: 又逐蠻直趣古鎮，過西延、大木諸洞，蠻人懾伏。

translations.literal: He again drove the barbarians straight toward Guzhen, passed through the caves of Xiyan, Damu, and others, and the barbarians submitted in awe.
translations.idiomatic: He then drove the tribes straight toward Guzhen, passing through the caves of Xiyan, Damu, and others until they submitted in fear.

sentences.zh: 淳化中，歷襄、鄧、宋、曹等州都巡檢使，改左監門衛將軍，屢部徒修護河防，改左領軍、左屯衛二將軍，充西京水南都巡檢使。

translations.literal: In the Chunhua era he successively served as metropolitan patrol commissioner of Xiang, Deng, Song, Cao, and other prefectures, was changed to general of the left Gate Guard, repeatedly led laborers in repairing river defenses, was changed to general of the left Leading and left Tunwei guards, and filled the post of southern patrol commissioner of the Western Capital on the waterways.
translations.idiomatic: During Chunhua he served in turn as metropolitan patrol commissioner of Xiang, Deng, Song, Cao, and other prefectures, became a general of the Left Gate Guard, repeatedly led crews in river defense work, was made general of the Left Leading and Left Tunwei guards, and served as southern patrol commissioner on the waterways of the Western Capital.

sentences.zh: 有盜掠彭婆鎮及甲馬營，延信馳以往，悉擒之。

translations.literal: When bandits plundered Pengpo town and the armor-and-horse camp, Yanxin rode there in haste and captured them all.
translations.idiomatic: When bandits raided Pengpo town and the armor-and-horse camp, Yanxin rode out at once and captured them all.

sentences.zh: 咸平中，歷太康、鞏縣二監軍。

translations.literal: In the Xianping era he successively served as military supervisor of Taikang and Gong counties.
translations.idiomatic: During Xianping he served in turn as military supervisor of Taikang and Gong counties.

sentences.zh: 景德二年，卒，年六十四。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jingde he died, aged sixty-four.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the second year of Jingde at the age of sixty-four.

sentences.zh: 程德玄

translations.literal: Cheng Dexuan
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Dexuan

sentences.zh: 程德玄，字禹錫，鄭州滎澤人。

translations.literal: Cheng Dexuan, style Yuxi, was a native of Xingze in Zhengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Dexuan, styled Yuxi, was from Xingze in Zheng Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 善醫術。

translations.literal: He was skilled in medicine.
translations.idiomatic: He was skilled in medicine.

sentences.zh: 太宗尹京邑，召置左右，署押衙，頗親信用事。

translations.literal: When Emperor Taizong governed the capital district he summoned him to attend at his side, appointed him aide-de-camp, and relied on him with considerable intimacy in affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taizong governed the capital, he summoned Dexuan to his side, appointed him aide-de-camp, and trusted him with considerable authority.

sentences.zh: 太祖大漸之夕，德玄宿信陵坊，夜有扣關疾呼趣赴宮邸者。

translations.literal: On the night when Emperor Taizu was critically ill, Dexuan was lodging in Xinling Ward; in the night someone knocked at the gate and urgently called for him to hurry to the princely residence.
translations.idiomatic: On the night the founding emperor lay gravely ill, Dexuan was staying in Xinling Ward when someone knocked at the gate and urgently summoned him to the prince's residence.

sentences.zh: 德玄遽起，不暇盥櫛，詣府，府門尚關。

translations.literal: Dexuan rose at once, without time to wash or comb his hair, and went to the residence, but the gate was still closed.
translations.idiomatic: Dexuan sprang up without time even to wash or comb his hair and hurried to the residence, but its gate was still shut.

sentences.zh: 方三鼓，德玄不自悟，盤桓久之。

translations.literal: It was just the third watch; Dexuan did not understand and lingered a long while.
translations.idiomatic: It was the third watch, and Dexuan, not understanding what was happening, lingered outside for a long time.

sentences.zh: 俄頃，見內侍王繼恩馳至，稱遺詔迎太宗即位。

translations.literal: Shortly he saw the inner attendant Wang Jien ride up, declaring that by the late emperor's testament Taizong was to be welcomed to ascend the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he saw the inner attendant Wang Jien ride up, announcing that by the late emperor's testament Taizong was to be brought in to succeed.

sentences.zh: 德玄因從以入，拜翰林使。

translations.literal: Dexuan therefore followed him in and was appointed Hanlin commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Dexuan followed him inside and was appointed Hanlin commissioner.

sentences.zh: 太平興國二年，陳洪進來朝，命德玄迎勞之。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taiping Xingguo, when Chen Hongjin came to court, Dexuan was ordered to go out to welcome and comfort him.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Taiping Xingguo, when Chen Hongjin came to court, Dexuan was sent to welcome and entertain him.

sentences.zh: 船艦度淮，暴風起，眾恐，皆請勿進。

translations.literal: As the fleet crossed the Huai, a violent wind arose; the crowd was afraid and all asked that they not advance.
translations.idiomatic: As the fleet crossed the Huai, a violent storm arose; the company was terrified and all urged that they turn back.

sentences.zh: 德玄曰：「吾將君命，豈避險？」

translations.literal: Dexuan said: "I bear the ruler's command—how could I avoid peril?"
translations.idiomatic: Dexuan said, "I carry the ruler's command—how can I shrink from danger?"

sentences.zh: 以酒祝而行，風浪遽止。

translations.literal: He offered a libation of wine and set out, and wind and waves abruptly ceased.
translations.idiomatic: He poured a libation and set out, and the wind and waves abruptly fell still.

sentences.zh: 三年，遷東上閤門使，兼翰林司事。

translations.literal: In the third year he was transferred to eastern upper Gate commissioner and concurrently directed Hanlin affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was made eastern upper Gate commissioner while also directing Hanlin affairs.

sentences.zh: 是秋，領代州刺史。

translations.literal: That autumn he held the prefecture of Daizhou.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn he was given Dai Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 從征太原，為行宮使，師還，以功改判四方館事。

translations.literal: He followed the campaign against Taiyuan as palace commissioner; when the army returned, for his merit he was changed to administer the Bureau of the Four Directions.
translations.idiomatic: He accompanied the campaign against Taiyuan as palace commissioner, and on the army's return was made administrator of the Bureau of the Four Directions for his service.

sentences.zh: 俄遷領本州團練使，又加領本州防禦使。

translations.literal: Shortly he was transferred to hold the regimental commander of his home prefecture and was further given the defense commissioner of that prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made regimental commander of his home prefecture and additionally defense commissioner there.

sentences.zh: 五年，坐市秦、隴竹木聯筏入京師，所過矯制免算，又高其估以入官，為王仁贍所發，責授東上閤門使，領本州刺史。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, because he marketed bamboo and timber from Qin and Long in linked rafts into the capital, along the way forged orders to exempt tolls, and also inflated valuations when entering goods to the state, he was exposed by Wang Renzan and demoted to eastern upper Gate commissioner while retaining the prefecture of his home commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was found to have floated rafts of Qin and Long bamboo and timber to the capital, forged orders along the route to evade tolls, and inflated valuations when turning goods over to the state. Exposed by Wang Renzan, he was demoted to eastern upper Gate commissioner while retaining his home prefecture.

sentences.zh: 陝府西南轉運使、左拾遺韋務升，京西轉運使、起居舍人程能，判官、右贊善大夫時載，坐縱德玄等於部下私販鬻，務升洎能並責授右贊善大夫，載將作監丞。

translations.literal: Wei Wusheng, left remonstrator and transport commissioner of southwestern Shaan prefecture, Cheng Neng, recorder of the left and transport commissioner of the western capital circuit, and Shi Zai, judge and right aide to the heir apparent, were punished for allowing Dexuan and others to engage in private trade and sale under them; Wusheng and Neng were both demoted to right aide to the heir apparent, and Zai to director of the Directorate of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Wusheng, left remonstrator and transport commissioner for southwestern Shaan, Cheng Neng, recorder of the left and transport commissioner for the western capital circuit, and Shi Zai, judge and right aide to the heir apparent, were punished for allowing Dexuan and others to trade privately under their jurisdiction. Wusheng and Neng were both demoted to right aides to the heir apparent, and Zai to director of the Directorate of Works.

sentences.zh: 是冬，車駕幸魏府，命總御營四面巡檢，掌給諸軍資糧。

translations.literal: That winter, when the imperial carriage visited Weifu, he was ordered to take overall command of patrol on all four sides of the imperial camp and to manage the supply of provisions to the armies.
translations.idiomatic: That winter, when the emperor visited We Prefecture, he was put in overall charge of patrol on all sides of the imperial camp and of provisioning the armies.

sentences.zh: 德玄攀附至近列，上頗信其言，繇是趨附者甚眾。

translations.literal: Dexuan had climbed by attachment to the inner ranks; the emperor quite trusted his words, and from this many rushed to attach themselves to him.
translations.idiomatic: Dexuan had risen by clinging to the inner circle, and the emperor came to trust his counsel, so many flocked to court his favor.

sentences.zh: 或言其交遊太盛，遂出為崇信軍節度行軍司馬。

translations.literal: Someone said his associations were too numerous, and he was therefore sent out as field marshal of the Chongxin military commission.
translations.idiomatic: When word spread that his circle of associates had grown too large, he was sent out as field marshal of the Chongxin command.

sentences.zh: 逾年，復拜慈州刺史，移知環州。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was again appointed prefect of Cizhou and transferred to govern Huanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he was again made prefect of Ci and transferred to govern Huan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 時西鄙酋豪相繼內附，詔以空名告敕百道付德玄，得便宜補授。

translations.literal: At the time tribal leaders on the western frontier submitted one after another; the court ordered that a hundred blank patents of appointment be given to Dexuan, with authority to appoint as circumstances required.
translations.idiomatic: As frontier chieftains on the western border submitted in succession, the court gave Dexuan a hundred blank patents of appointment with discretion to fill them as needed.

sentences.zh: 頃之，以疾求致仕，優詔不許。

translations.literal: Shortly he requested retirement on grounds of illness, but a gracious edict did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he asked to retire on account of illness, but a gracious edict refused permission.

sentences.zh: 淳化三年，改本州團練使、知邠州。

translations.literal: In the third year of Chunhua he was changed to regimental commander of his home prefecture and made administrator of Binzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Chunhua he was made regimental commander of his home prefecture and administrator of Bin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 未半歲，復典環州。

translations.literal: In less than half a year he was again put in charge of Huanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Within half a year he was again put in charge of Huan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 李順之寇西蜀，移知鳳州，兼領鳳、成、階、文等州駐泊兵馬事，徙慶州。

translations.literal: When Li Shun raided western Shu, he was transferred to govern Fengzhou, concurrently in charge of the stationed forces of Feng, Cheng, Jie, Wen, and other prefectures, then moved to Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Shun rebelled in western Shu, he was transferred to Feng Prefecture with concurrent charge of stationed troops in Feng, Cheng, Jie, Wen, and neighboring prefectures, then moved to Qing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 咸平中，入朝，真宗命坐撫勞，訪以邊事。

translations.literal: In the Xianping era he came to court; Emperor Zhenzong ordered him seated and comforted him, and questioned him about frontier affairs.
translations.idiomatic: During Xianping he came to court; Emperor Zhenzong had him seated, comforted him, and asked about frontier affairs.

sentences.zh: 俄出知幷州兼幷代副都部署，移鎮州，受代歸闕。

translations.literal: Shortly he went out as administrator of Bingzhou while also serving as deputy overall commander of Bing and Dai, was transferred to Zhenzhou, and on being relieved returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon sent out as prefect of Bing while also serving as deputy overall commander of Bing and Dai, then transferred to Zhen Prefecture, and on being relieved returned to court.

sentences.zh: 景德初，卒，年六十五。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jingde he died, aged sixty-five.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Jingde he died at the age of sixty-five.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符中，其子繼宗上章，懇祈贈典，上憫之，特贈鄭州防禦使。

translations.literal: In the Dazhong Xiangfu era his son Jizong submitted a memorial earnestly requesting posthumous honors; the emperor took pity and specially granted the title of defense commissioner of Zhengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: During Dazhong Xiangfu his son Jizong memorialized earnestly for posthumous honors; moved to pity, the emperor specially granted him the title of defense commissioner of Zheng Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 兄德元同仕王府，至內酒坊副使。

translations.literal: His elder brother Deyuan likewise served in the princely household and rose to deputy commissioner of the inner wine bureau.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Deyuan also served in the princely household and rose to deputy commissioner of the inner wine bureau.

sentences.zh: 繼宗，東頭供奉官、閤門祗候，次子繼忠，內殿崇班。

translations.literal: Jizong was eastern-head attendant-in-waiting and gate usher; his second son Jizhong was inner-palace honored guardsman.
translations.idiomatic: Jizong served as eastern-head attendant-in-waiting and gate usher; his second son Jizhong was an inner-palace honored guardsman.

sentences.zh: 德元子賁，大中祥符五年舉進士，累遷太常博士。

translations.literal: Deyuan's son Ben, in the fifth year of Dazhong Xiangfu passed the jinshi examination and was repeatedly promoted to erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Deyuan's son Ben passed the jinshi examination in the fifth year of Dazhong Xiangfu and rose in time to erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 王延德

translations.literal: Wang Yande
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yande

sentences.zh: 王延德，大名人。

translations.literal: Wang Yande was a native of Daming.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yande was from Daming.

sentences.zh: 少給事晉邸。

translations.literal: In youth he attended the household of the Prince of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth he served in the household of the Prince of Jin.

sentences.zh: 太平興國初，補殿前承旨，再遷供奉官。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taiping Xingguo he was appointed attendant of the Hall Forecourt and was twice promoted to attendant-in-waiting.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Taiping Xingguo he was made attendant of the Hall Forecourt and soon promoted twice to attendant-in-waiting.

sentences.zh: 六年，會高昌國遣使朝貢，太宗以遠人輸誠，遣延德與殿前承旨白勳使焉。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, when Gaochang sent envoys to offer tribute, Emperor Taizong, because distant people had shown sincerity, dispatched Yande together with forecourt attendant Bai Xun as envoys.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, when Gaochang sent tribute envoys, Emperor Taizong, moved by their distant sincerity, sent Yande with forecourt attendant Bai Xun as envoys in return.

sentences.zh: 自夏州渡河，經沙磧，歷伊州，望北庭萬五千里。

translations.literal: From Xiazhou they crossed the river, passed through sandy wastes, traversed Yizhou, and looked toward Beiting fifteen thousand li away.
translations.idiomatic: They crossed the river from Xia Prefecture, crossed the desert sands, passed through Yi Prefecture, and gazed toward Beiting fifteen thousand li distant.

sentences.zh: 雍熙二年，使還，撰《西州程記》以獻，授崇儀副使，掌御廚。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongxi the mission returned; he compiled the 《Record of the Journey to the Western Regions》 and presented it, was appointed deputy commissioner of honored guards, and managed the imperial kitchen.
translations.idiomatic: When the mission returned in the second year of Yongxi, he presented his 《Record of the Journey to the Western Regions》, was made deputy commissioner of honored guards, and put in charge of the imperial kitchen.

sentences.zh: 明年，拜正使，出知慶州。

translations.literal: The next year he was appointed full commissioner and went out as prefect of Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was made full commissioner and sent out as prefect of Qing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 淳化三年，代還，監折博倉。

translations.literal: In the third year of Chunhua, when relieved and returned, he supervised the exchange-and-trade granary.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Chunhua, on returning from his post, he was put in charge of the exchange-and-trade granary.

sentences.zh: 延德與張齊賢善，因國子博士朱貽業通言齊賢，求免掌庾，希進用。

translations.literal: Yande was on good terms with Zhang Qixian; through Guozijian erudite Zhu Yiye he conveyed word to Qixian asking to be relieved of managing the granary and hoping for advancement.
translations.idiomatic: Yande was friendly with Zhang Qixian and, through Guozijian erudite Zhu Yiye, asked Qixian to have him relieved of the granary post in hopes of promotion.

sentences.zh: 齊賢為言之，上怒曰：「延德願掌倉以自效，未逾月，又禱宰相求免，何也？」

translations.literal: Qixian spoke on his behalf; the emperor angrily said: "Yande wished to manage the granary to prove himself—within a month he is again praying the chief minister to be relieved; what is this?"
translations.idiomatic: Qixian spoke for him, and the emperor angrily said, "Yande asked to run the granary to prove himself, yet within a month he is begging the chief minister to be relieved—what is this?"

sentences.zh: 因召延德詰責，自言未嘗遣貽業詣相府有所求請。

translations.literal: He therefore summoned Yande to question and reproach him; Yande said himself that he had never sent Yiye to the chief minister's residence with any request.
translations.idiomatic: He summoned Yande to rebuke him; Yande insisted he had never sent Yiye to the chief minister's residence with any request.

sentences.zh: 上疑齊賢不實，召貽業至，貽業又諱之，齊賢恥自辨，因頓首稱罪。

translations.literal: The emperor suspected Qixian was not truthful, summoned Yiye, and Yiye again concealed the matter; Qixian was ashamed to defend himself and therefore kowtowed and confessed guilt.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor suspected Qixian was lying, summoned Yiye, and Yiye again denied it. Ashamed to argue his case, Qixian simply kowtowed and confessed fault.

sentences.zh: 上怒，即以延德領懿州刺史以寵之。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry and thereupon had Yande hold the prefecture of Yizhou as a mark of favor.
translations.idiomatic: Still angry, the emperor made Yande prefect of Yi Prefecture as a mark of favor.

sentences.zh: 五年，提點三司衙司、磨勘憑由司。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was made overseer of the Three Offices yamen and the credentials examination bureau.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was made overseer of the Three Offices yamen and the credentials examination bureau.

sentences.zh: 未幾，拜左屯衛大將軍、樞密都承旨，俄授度支使。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed great general of the left Tunwei guard and overall bearer of the Privy Council, and shortly was given the fiscal commission.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was made great general of the Left Tunwei Guard and overall bearer of the Privy Council, and soon afterward fiscal commissioner.

sentences.zh: 延德以攀附得官，傾險好進，時人惡之。

translations.literal: Yande had gained office by clinging to patrons; he was overreaching and eager to advance, and people of the time detested him.
translations.idiomatic: Yande had risen by currying favor; overreaching and ambitious, he was widely disliked.

sentences.zh: 兄延之，乾德六年進士，至屯田郎中致仕。

translations.literal: His elder brother Yanzhi, jinshi in the sixth year of Qiande, rose to director of the agricultural lands bureau and retired.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Yanzhi, a jinshi of the sixth year of Qiande, rose to director of the agricultural lands bureau before retiring.

sentences.zh: 張質，字守樸，博州高唐人。

translations.literal: Zhang Zhi, styled Shoupu, was a man of Gaotang in Bozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhi, styled Shoupu, was from Gaotang in Bozhou.

sentences.zh: 少孤，養於兄讚。

translations.literal: He lost his father young and was raised by his elder brother Zan.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned in youth, he was brought up by his elder brother Zan.

sentences.zh: 讚為樞密院典謁，質因得隸兵房，頗為趙普、曹彬所知。

translations.literal: Zan was a reception clerk at the Bureau of Military Affairs; Zhi thereby came to serve in the military affairs section and was well regarded by Zhao Pu and Cao Bin.
translations.idiomatic: Zan served as a reception clerk at the Bureau of Military Affairs, and Zhi thereby entered the military affairs section, where he won considerable notice from Zhao Pu and Cao Bin.

sentences.zh: 太宗征河東，還駐鎮陽，彬方典樞務。

translations.literal: When Emperor Taizong campaigned against Hedong and returned to encamp at Zhenyang, Bin was then directing affairs at the Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taizong marched against Hedong and returned to encamp at Zhenyang, Cao Bin was then in charge of Bureau affairs.

sentences.zh: 一夕，議調發屯兵，時，軍載簿領，阻留在道。

translations.literal: One evening they deliberated on mobilizing garrison troops; at the time military transport ledgers were held up on the road.
translations.idiomatic: One evening the court deliberated mobilizing garrison troops, but the military transport ledgers were stalled on the road.

sentences.zh: 質潛計兵數，部分軍馬，及得兵籍較之，悉無差謬。

translations.literal: Zhi secretly calculated troop numbers, assigned portions of armies and horses, and when he obtained the military registers and compared them, there were no discrepancies at all.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi quietly reckoned the troop totals, apportioned armies and horses, and when the military registers arrived for comparison, every figure matched without error.

sentences.zh: 淳化中，累遷本房副都承旨。

translations.literal: In the Chunhua era he was repeatedly promoted to deputy associate director of his section.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chunhua reign he rose step by step to deputy associate director of his section.

sentences.zh: 咸平初，授左監門衛將軍、樞密副都承旨。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xianping he was appointed general of the Left Gate Guard Corps and deputy associate director of the Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Xianping reign he was made general of the Left Gate Guard Corps and deputy associate director of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 先是，樞密吏皆以年勞次補，有至主事而懵其職者。

translations.literal: Previously, clerks at the Bureau of Military Affairs had all been appointed by seniority in years of service; some reached section chief yet remained ignorant of their duties.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Bureau clerks had all been promoted by length of service in order; some rose as high as section chief without understanding their work.

sentences.zh: 景德三年夏，內出公事三條，令主事以下詳決之，命質與禮房副承旨尹德潤宿御書院考第。

translations.literal: In the summer of the third year of Jingde, three official matters were issued from within the palace ordering detailed adjudication by those below section chief; Zhi and Yin Derun, deputy attendant of the Rites Section, were ordered to lodge at the Imperial Library Academy to grade them.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of Jingde 3, the palace issued three official cases for adjudication by all ranks below section chief, and ordered Zhi and Yin Derun, deputy attendant of the Rites Section, to stay at the Imperial Library Academy and grade the candidates.

sentences.zh: 翌日，上親臨閱視，凡選補四十餘人，不中式除崇班、供奉官、奉職者十餘人。

translations.literal: The next day the emperor came in person to review; altogether more than forty were selected for appointment; more than ten who failed the examination were removed from the Honored Corps, palace attendant officers, and attendants-in-service.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the emperor reviewed the results in person. More than forty were chosen for promotion, while more than ten who failed were stripped of their ranks in the Honored Corps, as palace attendants, and as attendants-in-service.

sentences.zh: 以質為左屯衛大將軍，加給月奉，歷右神武軍、右衛二大將軍。

translations.literal: Zhi was made grand general of the Left Garrison Guard Corps, given an additional monthly stipend, and served successively as grand general of the Right Divine Martial Army and Right Guard Corps.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi was appointed grand general of the Left Garrison Guard Corps with an added monthly stipend, and later served as grand general of both the Right Divine Martial Army and the Right Guard Corps.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符七年，轉都承旨。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Dazhong Xiangfu he was transferred to associate director.
translations.idiomatic: In Dazhong Xiangfu 7 he was promoted to associate director.

sentences.zh: 在樞要僅五十日，練習事程，精敏端愨，未嘗有過。

translations.literal: In the crucial post for only fifty days, he mastered the routines of business—sharp, diligent, and upright—and never once committed an error.
translations.idiomatic: Though he held this crucial post for only fifty days, he mastered every routine of the office—keen, efficient, and upright—and never once faltered.

sentences.zh: 舊，本院吏罕有遷至都承旨者，上素知質廉謹，故以授之。

translations.literal: Formerly, clerks of the Bureau rarely rose to associate director; the emperor had long known Zhi's integrity and prudence, and therefore entrusted him with the post.
translations.idiomatic: Seldom before had a Bureau clerk risen to associate director, but the emperor had long known Zhi for his integrity and carefulness, and so gave him the appointment.

sentences.zh: 嘗召問五代以降洎國初軍籍更易之制，且命條具利害，質纂為三篇，目曰《兵要》以進，上覽而稱善。

translations.literal: He was once summoned and questioned about systems for changes to military registers from the Five Dynasties down through the founding of the dynasty, and also ordered to itemize advantages and disadvantages; Zhi compiled three chapters titled 《Essentials of Warfare》 and presented them; the emperor read them and praised them.
translations.idiomatic: He was once summoned to explain how military registers had been altered from the Five Dynasties through the dynasty's founding, and ordered to set out the pros and cons in detail. Zhi compiled three chapters under the title 《Essentials of Warfare》 and submitted them; the emperor read the work and commended it.

sentences.zh: 楊允恭

translations.literal: Yang Yungong
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yungong

sentences.zh: 楊允恭，漢州綿竹人。

translations.literal: Yang Yungong was a man of Mianzhu in Han Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yungong was from Mianzhu in Han Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 家世豪富，允恭少倜儻任俠。

translations.literal: His family had been wealthy for generations; Yungong in youth was free-spirited and chivalrous.
translations.idiomatic: His family had been rich for generations, and in youth Yungong was bold, unconventional, and fond of deeds of chivalry.

sentences.zh: 乾德中，王師平蜀，群盜竊發，允恭裁弱冠，率鄉里子弟砦於清泉鄉，為賊所獲，將殺之。

translations.literal: In the Qiande era, when the imperial army pacified Shu, bandits rose everywhere; Yungong had just reached adulthood and led local youths to fortify at Qingquan Township; they were captured by bandits and were about to be killed.
translations.idiomatic: During Qiande, as the imperial army pacified Shu, bandits broke out on every side. Yungong had only just come of age when he led local youths to fortify Qingquan Township; the bandits captured them and were about to execute him.

sentences.zh: 允恭曰：「苟活我，當助爾。」

translations.literal: Yungong said: "If you spare my life, I will help you."
translations.idiomatic: Yungong said, "If you let me live, I will aid you."

sentences.zh: 賊素聞其豪宗，乃釋之。

translations.literal: The bandits had long heard of his great clan, and so they released him.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits had long known his family as a powerful local house, and so they set him free.

sentences.zh: 陰結賊帥子，日與飲博，陽不勝，償以貲，使伺賊。

translations.literal: He secretly allied with the bandit chief's son, drinking and gambling with him daily; he would feign losing and pay with goods, using this to spy on the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: He secretly befriended the bandit chief's son, drinking and gambling with him every day; he would deliberately lose and pay his stakes in goods, all the while watching the bandits' movements.

sentences.zh: 賊將害允恭，其子以告，因遁去。

translations.literal: The bandits were about to kill Yungong; the chief's son told him, and he fled in secret.
translations.idiomatic: When the bandits were about to kill Yungong, the chief's son warned him, and he escaped in secret.

sentences.zh: 內客省使丁德裕討賊至州，允恭以策幹之，署綿、漢招收巡檢，賊平，補殿前承旨。

translations.literal: When Ding Deyu, commissioner of the Inner Reception Bureau, came to the prefecture to suppress the bandits, Yungong presented his stratagem; he was appointed recruitment and inspection commissioner for Mian and Han; when the bandits were pacified he was appointed palace front attendant.
translations.idiomatic: When Ding Deyu, commissioner of the Inner Reception Bureau, arrived in the prefecture to suppress the bandits, Yungong offered his plan and was appointed recruitment and inspection commissioner for Mian and Han. After the bandits were pacified, he was made a palace front attendant.

sentences.zh: 太平興國中，以殿直掌廣州市舶。

translations.literal: In the Taiping Xingguo era, as a palace attendant he managed Guangzhou maritime trade.
translations.idiomatic: During Taiping Xingguo he served as a palace attendant in charge of Guangzhou maritime trade.

sentences.zh: 自南漢之後，海賊子孫相襲，大者及數百人，州縣苦之。

translations.literal: Since Southern Han, pirates had passed their trade from generation to generation; the largest bands numbered several hundred men, and prefectures and counties suffered from them.
translations.idiomatic: Since the time of Southern Han, piracy had passed from father to son; the largest bands numbered several hundred men, and prefectures and counties were hard pressed by them.

sentences.zh: 允恭因部運入奏其事，太宗即命為廣、連都巡檢使。

translations.literal: Yungong reported on this when he returned to court with a transport mission; Emperor Taizong immediately appointed him chief inspection commissioner of Guang and Lian.
translations.idiomatic: When Yungong returned to court on a transport mission and reported the situation, Emperor Taizong immediately appointed him chief inspection commissioner of Guang and Lian.

sentences.zh: 又以海鹽盜入嶺北，民犯者眾，請建大庾縣為軍，官輦鹽市之。

translations.literal: Moreover, because sea salt was smuggled north of the Nanling Mountains and many commoners violated the ban, he requested that Dayu County be established as a military prefecture and that the government transport salt there for sale.
translations.idiomatic: Because sea salt was being smuggled north of the Nanling Mountains and violations were widespread, he also asked that Dayu County be elevated to a military prefecture where the government could haul in salt and sell it.

sentences.zh: 詔建為南安軍，自是冒禁者少。

translations.literal: An edict established it as Nan'an Military Prefecture; from then on violators of the prohibition were fewer.
translations.idiomatic: An edict created Nan'an Military Prefecture, and from that time violations of the salt ban grew fewer.

sentences.zh: 賊有葉氏者，眾五百餘，往來海上。

translations.literal: There was a band of the Ye clan numbering more than five hundred who traveled back and forth on the sea.
translations.idiomatic: One pirate band, the Ye clan, numbered more than five hundred men and ranged back and forth across the sea.

sentences.zh: 允恭集水軍，造輕舠，掩襲其首，斬之。

translations.literal: Yungong assembled naval forces, built light boats, and launched a surprise raid on their leader and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Yungong gathered a naval force, built light craft, and launched a surprise attack on the band's leader, whom he beheaded.

sentences.zh: 餘黨棄船走，伏匿山谷，允恭伐木開道，悉殲焉。

translations.literal: The remaining followers abandoned their ships and fled, hiding in mountain valleys; Yungong cut trees to open paths and exterminated them all.
translations.idiomatic: The survivors abandoned their ships and fled into the mountains; Yungong cut timber to open paths and wiped them out to the last man.

sentences.zh: 賊寇每遇風濤，則遁止洲島間。

translations.literal: Whenever pirates met wind and waves they would flee and halt among islands and sandbars.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever pirates ran into wind and heavy seas, they would take refuge among islands and sandbars.

sentences.zh: 允恭領眾涉海，捕之殆盡，賊皆望風奔潰。

translations.literal: Yungong led his men across the sea and captured nearly all of them; the bandits all fled at sight of his forces.
translations.idiomatic: Yungong led his men across the sea and hunted them down almost to extinction; thereafter the pirates fled at the mere sight of his banners.

sentences.zh: 又抵漳、泉賊所止處，盡奪先所劫男女六十餘口還其家。

translations.literal: He also reached places where Zhang and Quan pirates had halted and fully recovered more than sixty men and women they had earlier seized, returning them to their families.
translations.idiomatic: He also tracked pirates to their haunts in Zhang and Quan, recovered more than sixty men and women they had seized, and sent them home.

sentences.zh: 詔書嘉獎，賜錢十萬，轉供奉官。

translations.literal: An edict commended and rewarded him, granting one hundred thousand cash and promoting him to palace attendant officer.
translations.idiomatic: An imperial edict praised his service, granted him one hundred thousand cash, and promoted him to palace attendant officer.

sentences.zh: 詔歸，改內殿崇班。

translations.literal: Ordered to return to court, he was changed to the Inner Hall Honored Corps.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled to court, he was transferred to the Inner Hall Honored Corps.

sentences.zh: 時緣江多賊，命督江南水運，因捕寇黨。

translations.literal: At the time there were many bandits along the Yangtze; he was ordered to supervise Jiangnan water transport and thereby capture outlaw bands.
translations.idiomatic: Because bandits were rife along the Yangtze, he was ordered to supervise Jiangnan water transport and capture outlaw bands in the course of his duties.

sentences.zh: 行及臨江軍，擇驍卒輕舟伺下江賊所止，夜發軍城，三鼓，遇賊百餘，拒敵久之，悉梟其首。

translations.literal: When he reached Linjiang Military Prefecture, he selected elite soldiers in light boats to reconnoiter where downstream bandits halted; at night he set out from the garrison city; at the third watch he encountered more than a hundred bandits; after long fighting he beheaded them all.
translations.idiomatic: At Linjiang Military Prefecture he chose elite troops in light boats to scout where downstream bandits were hiding. Setting out from the garrison city at night, at the third watch he met more than a hundred bandits; after a long fight he beheaded them all.

sentences.zh: 又趣通州境上躡海賊，賊係眾舟。

translations.literal: He also hastened to the border of Tong Prefecture to track sea pirates; the bandits had chained their boats together.
translations.idiomatic: He then hurried to the Tong Prefecture frontier to pursue sea pirates, who had lashed their boats together in a line.

sentences.zh: 張幕，發勁弩、短炮。

translations.literal: They stretched screens and deployed powerful crossbows and short catapults.
translations.idiomatic: They stretched protective screens and opened fire with powerful crossbows and short catapults.

sentences.zh: 允恭兵刃所向，多為幕所縈，炮中允恭左肩，流血及袖，容色彌壯。

translations.literal: Wherever Yungong's soldiers struck, they were often entangled by the screens; a catapult bolt struck his left shoulder; blood soaked his sleeve, yet his bearing grew only firmer.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever Yungong's men thrust, they were often snared by the screens. A catapult bolt struck his left shoulder and blood ran down his sleeve, yet his expression grew only fiercer.

sentences.zh: 徐遣善泅者以繩連鐵鉤散擲之，壞其幕，士卒爭進，賊赴水死者大半，擒數百人。

translations.literal: He calmly sent skilled swimmers to attach ropes to iron hooks and scatter-throw them, destroying the screens; the soldiers vied to press forward; more than half the bandits drowned fleeing into the water, and several hundred were captured.
translations.idiomatic: He calmly sent skilled swimmers to throw iron hooks tied to ropes and tear the screens apart; his soldiers surged forward, more than half the bandits drowned trying to escape into the water, and several hundred were taken alive.

sentences.zh: 自是江路無剽掠之患。

translations.literal: From then on the river route was free of the scourge of plunder.
translations.idiomatic: After that the river routes were free of piracy.

sentences.zh: 以功轉洛苑副使，江、淮、兩浙都大發運、擘畫茶鹽捕賊事；

translations.literal: For his merit he was transferred to deputy commissioner of the Luoyang Imperial Park, Grand Transport Commissioner for Jianghuai and the Two Zhes, with charge over planning tea, salt, and pirate suppression;
translations.idiomatic: For his achievements he was made deputy commissioner of the Luoyang Imperial Park and Grand Transport Commissioner for Jianghuai and the Two Zhes, with authority over tea, salt, and pirate suppression;

sentences.zh: 賜紫袍、金帶、錢五十萬。

translations.literal: he was granted a purple robe, a gold belt, and five hundred thousand cash.
translations.idiomatic: and was granted a purple robe, a gold belt, and five hundred thousand cash.

sentences.zh: 先是，三路轉運使各領其職，或廩庾多積，而軍士舟楫不給，雖以官錢雇丁男挽舟，而土人憚其役，以是歲上供米，不過三百萬。

translations.literal: Previously the transport commissioners of the three routes each held their own jurisdiction; sometimes granaries held large stores yet soldiers' boats and supplies were insufficient; although official funds hired laborers to haul boats, local people feared the corvée—thus the annual tribute of rice to the capital did not exceed three million.
translations.idiomatic: Previously the transport commissioners of the three routes each managed his own circuit. Granaries might be full while boats and supplies for the troops remained inadequate; although official funds were used to hire laborers to haul barges, local people dreaded the corvée, so the annual rice delivered to the capital did not exceed three million piculs.

sentences.zh: 允恭盡籍三路舟卒與所運物數，令諸州擇牙吏，悉集，允恭乃辨數授之。

translations.literal: Yungong fully registered the boat crews and cargo counts of the three routes, ordered each prefecture to select clerks, gathered them all together, and then assigned numbers by sorting.
translations.idiomatic: Yungong fully registered the boat crews and cargo totals of all three routes, had each prefecture choose clerks, gathered them together, and then assigned each his quota by careful reckoning.

sentences.zh: 江、浙所運，止於淮、泗，由淮、泗輸京師，行之一歲，上供者六百萬。

translations.literal: What Jiang and Zhe transported stopped at Huai and Si; from Huai and Si it was sent to the capital; after one year of operation, tribute reached six million.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang and Zhe shipments now stopped at Huai and Si, whence grain went on to the capital. After one year under the new system, tribute deliveries reached six million piculs.

sentences.zh: 淳化五年，轉西京作坊使。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Chunhua he was transferred to commissioner of the Western Capital Workshops.
translations.idiomatic: In Chunhua 5 he was made commissioner of the Western Capital Workshops.

sentences.zh: 初，產茶之地，民輸賦者悉計其直，官售之，精粗不校，咸輸榷務。

translations.literal: Initially, in tea-producing regions the tax grain commoners submitted was all calculated at fixed value and sold to the government, which did not distinguish fine from coarse; all was delivered to monopoly offices.
translations.idiomatic: At first, in tea-producing districts the grain tax was calculated at a fixed cash value and sold to the government, which made no distinction between fine and coarse grades; all of it went to the monopoly offices.

sentences.zh: 商人弗肯售，久即焚之。

translations.literal: Merchants would not buy it; after long storage it was burned.
translations.idiomatic: Merchants refused to buy it, and after long storage it was burned.

sentences.zh: 允恭曰：「竭民利而取之，積腐而棄之，非善計也。」

translations.literal: Yungong said: "To exhaust the people's profit in taking it, pile it until it rots and discard it—this is no good policy."
translations.idiomatic: Yungong said, "To squeeze the people dry in collecting tea, stockpile it until it rots, and then throw it away—this is no sound policy."

sentences.zh: 至道初，劉式建議請廢緣江榷務，許商人過江，聽私貨鬻。

translations.literal: In the early Zhidao reign Liu Shi proposed abolishing the Yangtze monopoly offices, allowing merchants to cross the river and sell private goods freely.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Zhidao reign Liu Shi proposed abolishing the Yangtze monopoly offices and allowing merchants to cross the river and sell tea freely.

sentences.zh: 允恭以為諸州新陳相糅，兩河諸州風土，各有所宜，非雜以數品，即商人少利。

translations.literal: Yungong held that the new and old stock of the various prefectures was intermixed, and the soils and climates of the prefectures of the two He regions each had what suited them; unless several grades were mixed together merchants would gain little profit.
translations.idiomatic: Yungong argued that stocks of new and old tea were mingled among the prefectures, and that the soils of the Two He regions each suited different grades; unless several varieties were blended, merchants would see little profit.

sentences.zh: 請依舊江北置務，均色號，以年次給之。

translations.literal: He requested that offices be established north of the river as before, grades standardized, and tea distributed by year order.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that monopoly offices be restored north of the river as before, grades standardized, and tea issued by vintage.

sentences.zh: 事下三司，鹽鐵使陳恕等以允恭議為是，詔從之。

translations.literal: The matter was sent to the Three Offices; Salt and Iron Commissioner Chen Shu and others approved Yungong's proposal, and an edict followed it.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal went to the Three Offices; Salt and Iron Commissioner Chen Shu and others endorsed Yungong's plan, and an edict adopted it.

sentences.zh: 即命允恭為發運使，始改「擘畫」為「制置」，以西京作坊副使李廷遂、著作佐郎王子輿並為同發運使。

translations.literal: Yungong was immediately appointed transport commissioner; the title was first changed from "Planning" to "Regulation"; Li Tingsui, deputy commissioner of the Western Capital Workshops, and Wang Ziyu, assistant editor, were both made co-transport commissioners.
translations.idiomatic: Yungong was immediately appointed transport commissioner, and the title was changed from "Planning" to "Regulation." Li Tingsui, deputy commissioner of the Western Capital Workshops, and Wang Ziyu, assistant editor, were appointed co-transport commissioners.

sentences.zh: 巢、廬江二縣舊隸廬州，道遠多寇，民輸勞費。

translations.literal: Chao and Lujiang counties had formerly been subordinate to Luzhou; the road was long and bandits numerous, and the people suffered labor and expense in delivery.
translations.idiomatic: Chao and Lujiang counties had long been subordinate to Luzhou; the route was long, bandits were many, and the people bore heavy costs in delivering their taxes.

sentences.zh: 允恭請以二縣建軍，詔許之，以無為為額。

translations.literal: Yungong requested that the two counties be established as a military prefecture; an edict granted it, taking Wuwei as the name.
translations.idiomatic: Yungong asked that the two counties be made a military prefecture; the court approved, naming it Wuwei.

sentences.zh: 淮南十八州軍，其九禁鹽地，則上下其直，民利商鹽之賤，故販者益眾，至有持兵器往來為盜者。

translations.literal: Of the eighteen prefectures and armies of Huainan, nine were salt-monopoly zones; prices were raised and lowered there; commoners profited from cheap merchant salt, so smugglers grew ever more numerous, until some traveled to and fro bearing weapons as bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Of Huainan's eighteen prefectures and armies, nine were government salt-monopoly zones where prices were adjusted up and down. Because commoners profited from cheap merchant salt, smugglers grew ever more numerous, until some went about armed as bandits.

sentences.zh: 允恭以為行法宜一，即奏請悉禁，而官遣吏主之。

translations.literal: Yungong held that the law ought to be uniform; he immediately memorialized requesting a full prohibition, with officials dispatched to manage it.
translations.idiomatic: Yungong held that the law should be uniform throughout the region and immediately memorialized asking that private salt be fully prohibited and managed by officials sent by the government.

sentences.zh: 事下三司，三司言其不可，允恭再三為請，太宗始從之。

translations.literal: The matter was sent to the Three Offices; the Three Offices said it could not be done; Yungong repeatedly petitioned, and Emperor Taizong finally agreed.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal went to the Three Offices, which declared it unworkable, but Yungong petitioned again and again until Emperor Taizong at last consented.

sentences.zh: 是歲，收利巨萬。

translations.literal: That year profits collected amounted to tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: That year revenues ran to tens of thousands of strings of cash.

sentences.zh: 允恭與王子輿、秦羲同主茶鹽之任，多作條製，遂變新法。

translations.literal: Yungong, together with Wang Ziyu and Qin Xi, jointly held charge of tea and salt affairs; they made many regulations and thereby changed the new law.
translations.idiomatic: Yungong, Wang Ziyu, and Qin Xi jointly directed tea and salt policy, drafting many new regulations and thereby remaking the system.

sentences.zh: 俄知通利軍，兼黃、御河發運使。

translations.literal: Soon he was made military prefect of Tongli and concurrently transport commissioner of the Huang and Imperial Canals.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was made military prefect of Tongli and concurrently transport commissioner for the Huang and Imperial Canals.

sentences.zh: 會議減西鄙屯兵，以息轉餉，召允恭與崇儀副使竇神寶、閣門祗候李允則馳往經度，圖上郡縣山川之形勝。

translations.literal: When the court deliberated reducing garrison troops on the western frontier to cease supply transport, Yungong was summoned together with Vice Commissioner Dou Shenbao and Gate Attendant Li Yunze to hurry there and survey the terrain, submitting maps of the strategic advantages of the commanderies, counties, mountains, and rivers.
translations.idiomatic: When the court debated reducing frontier garrisons in the west to cut supply costs, Yungong was summoned together with Vice Commissioner Dou Shenbao and Gate Attendant Li Yunze to ride post-haste and survey the region, submitting maps of the strategic terrain of its commanderies, counties, mountains, and rivers.

sentences.zh: 允恭因建議曰：「自環州入積石、抵靈武七日程。

translations.literal: Yungong thereupon memorialized, saying: "From Huanzhou entering Jishi and reaching Lingwu is a journey of seven days.
translations.idiomatic: Yungong thereupon proposed, "From Huanzhou through Jishi to Lingwu is a march of seven days.

sentences.zh: 芻粟之運，其策有三。

translations.literal: For the transport of forage and grain, there are three strategies.
translations.idiomatic: There are three ways to move forage and grain.

sentences.zh: 然以人以驢，其費頗煩，而所載數鮮。

translations.literal: Yet whether by men or by donkeys, the expense is quite troublesome and the quantity carried is rarely great.
translations.idiomatic: But whether by men or by donkeys, the cost is heavy and the loads are small.

sentences.zh: 莫若用諸葛亮木牛之制，以小車發卒分鋪運之。

translations.literal: Better to use Zhuge Liang's wooden-ox design, sending out small carts with soldiers stationed at relays to transport it.
translations.idiomatic: Better to adopt Zhuge Liang's wooden-ox carts, using small wagons and relay teams of soldiers to move supplies along the route.

sentences.zh: 每一車四人挽之，旁設兵衛，加戈刃於其上，寇至則聚車於中，合士卒之力，禦寇於外。」

translations.literal: Each cart would be pulled by four men; guards would be posted alongside and spear-blades mounted on top; when bandits come the carts would be gathered in the center and the soldiers would combine their strength to repel the bandits from without."
translations.idiomatic: Each cart would be hauled by four men, with guards posted alongside and weapons mounted on the wagons. When raiders appear, the carts would be drawn into a circle and the soldiers would combine to fight them off from within."

sentences.zh: 尋為議者所沮而止。

translations.literal: Soon afterward it was blocked by critics and abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: The plan was soon blocked by critics and dropped.

sentences.zh: 復遣之任，又議，江、淮鹽鐵使陳恕力爭，詔從允恭之議。

translations.literal: He was again dispatched to his post; when the matter was again deliberated, Jianghuai Salt and Iron Commissioner Chen Shu argued forcefully; an edict followed Yungong's proposal.
translations.idiomatic: Yungong was sent back to his post, and when the matter was debated again, Jianghuai Salt and Iron Commissioner Chen Shu argued strenuously; an edict adopted Yungong's view.

sentences.zh: 加領康州刺史。

translations.literal: He was additionally put in charge of Kang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was additionally made prefect of Kangzhou.

sentences.zh: 咸平初，以北邊賣馬，未有定直，命允恭主平其估，乃置估馬司，鑄印以為常制。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xianping, because there was no fixed price for selling horses on the northern frontier, Yungong was ordered to set fair appraisals; he thereupon established a horse-appraisal office and cast a seal as a permanent regulation.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Xianping, because frontier horse sales had no fixed price, Yungong was ordered to establish fair valuations; he set up a horse-appraisal office and cast an official seal as a standing rule.

sentences.zh: 王均之亂，上慮南方有聚寇，命允恭為荊湖、江、浙都巡檢使，內殿崇班楊守遵副之，賜與甚厚。

translations.literal: During Wang Jun's rebellion the emperor feared bandits might gather in the south and appointed Yungong chief inspection commissioner of Jinghu, Jiang, and Zhe; Yang Shouzun of the Inner Hall Honored Corps served as his deputy; grants and gifts were very generous.
translations.idiomatic: During Wang Jun's rebellion the emperor feared bandits might gather in the south and appointed Yungong chief inspection commissioner of Jinghu, Jiang, and Zhe, with Yang Shouzun of the Inner Hall Honored Corps as his deputy; the gifts bestowed on him were lavish.

sentences.zh: 二年夏，以疾聞，遣其子大理評事可乘傳侍疾。

translations.literal: In the second year, summer, word of illness reached the court; his son Ke, court reviewer, was ordered to travel post-haste to attend him in his illness.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, summer, word of his illness reached court, and his son Ke, a court reviewer, was sent by express relay to nurse him.

sentences.zh: 七月，卒於升州，年五十六，賜其次子告同學究出身，賻錢二十萬、絹百匹。

translations.literal: In the seventh month he died at Shengzhou, aged fifty-six; his second son Gao was granted Academician Emeritus status, with funeral gifts of two hundred thousand cash and one hundred bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month he died at Shengzhou, aged fifty-six. His second son Gao was granted Academician Emeritus status, with funeral gifts of two hundred thousand cash and one hundred bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 又以錢五萬、帛五十匹給其家。

translations.literal: An additional fifty thousand cash and fifty bolts of silk were given to his family.
translations.idiomatic: The court also gave his family fifty thousand cash and fifty bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 命揚州官造第一區賜之。

translations.literal: Officials of Yang Prefecture were ordered to build a foremost residence and grant it to them.
translations.idiomatic: Officials in Yang Prefecture were ordered to build a first-rank residence and grant it to the family.

sentences.zh: 允恭有膽幹，能以方略捕賊。

translations.literal: Yungong had courage and capability and could capture bandits by strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Yungong was bold and resourceful and knew how to capture bandits by stratagem.

sentences.zh: 王小波之亂也，李順之兄自榮據綿竹，土人多被脅從。

translations.literal: During Wang Xiaobo's rebellion, Li Shun's elder brother Zirong held Mianzhu; many local people were coerced into joining him.
translations.idiomatic: During Wang Xiaobo's rebellion, Li Shun's elder brother Zirong seized Mianzhu, and many locals were forced to follow him.

sentences.zh: 允恭兄允升、弟允元，率鄉里子弟並力破之；

translations.literal: Yungong's elder brother Yunsheng and younger brother Yunyuan led local youths and together broke them;
translations.idiomatic: Yungong's elder brother Yunsheng and younger brother Yunyuan rallied local youths and together defeated them;

sentences.zh: 又為王師鄉導，執自榮詣劍門以獻。

translations.literal: they also served as local guides for the imperial army, seized Zirong, and presented him at Jianmen Pass.
translations.idiomatic: they also guided the imperial army, captured Zirong, and brought him to Jianmen Pass as a prisoner.

sentences.zh: 王繼恩表其事，詔賜允升學究出身，授本縣令，允元什邡令。

translations.literal: Wang Jien memorialized the affair; an edict granted Yunsheng Academician Emeritus status and appointed him magistrate of his home county; Yunyuan was made magistrate of Shifang.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jien reported the affair to court; an edict granted Yunsheng Academician Emeritus status and made him magistrate of his home county, and appointed Yunyuan magistrate of Shifang.

sentences.zh: 明年，召赴闕，授允升右讚善大夫，允元大理評事。

translations.literal: The next year they were summoned to court; Yunsheng was appointed Right Supporter of Goodness Grandee and Yunyuan court reviewer.
translations.idiomatic: The next year they were summoned to court; Yunsheng was made Right Supporter of Goodness Grandee and Yunyuan a court reviewer.

sentences.zh: 可，咸平元年進士，喜屬文，有吏幹，累召試，曆戶部、鹽鐵判官，知洪、宣、潤、壽、潭州，至都官員外郎。

translations.literal: Ke, jinshi of the first year of Xianping, delighted in literary composition and had administrative talent; repeatedly called to examinations; he served successively as judicial officer in the Ministry of Revenue and Salt and Iron; governed Hong, Xuan, Run, Shou, and Tan prefectures; rose to vice director of the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Ke, a jinshi of Xianping 1, loved literary composition and had a gift for administration. Repeatedly summoned to court examinations, he served as judicial officer in the Ministry of Revenue and Salt and Iron, governed Hong, Xuan, Run, Shou, and Tan prefectures, and rose to vice director of the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 告，虞部員外郎。

translations.literal: Gao, vice director of the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Gao served as vice director of the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 秦羲，字致堯，江寧人。

translations.literal: Qin Xi, styled Zhiyao, was a man of Jiangning.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Xi, styled Zhiyao, was from Jiangning.

sentences.zh: 世仕江左。

translations.literal: His family had served the lower Yangtze for generations.
translations.idiomatic: His family had held office south of the Yangtze for generations.

sentences.zh: 曾祖本，岳州刺史。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Ben was prefect of Yuezhou.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Ben served as prefect of Yuezhou.

sentences.zh: 祖進遠，寧國軍節度副使。

translations.literal: His grandfather Jinyuan was vice military commissioner of Ningguo Army.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Jinyuan was vice military commissioner of the Ningguo Army.

sentences.zh: 父承裕，建州監軍使、知州事。

translations.literal: His father Chengyu was military supervisor of Jianzhou and acting prefect.
translations.idiomatic: His father Chengyu was military supervisor of Jianzhou and acting prefect.

sentences.zh: 李煜之歸朝也，承裕遣羲詣闕上符印，太祖召見，悅其趨對詳謹，補殿直，令督廣濟漕船。

translations.literal: When Li Yu submitted to the dynasty Chengyu sent Xi to court to present credentials and seals; Emperor Taizu summoned him, pleased with his detailed and careful responses; he was appointed palace attendant and ordered to supervise Guangji transport boats.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Yu surrendered to the Song, Chengyu sent Xi to court to present the seals and credentials. Emperor Taizu received him, pleased by his careful and thorough replies, appointed him a palace attendant, and put him in charge of Guangji transport boats.

sentences.zh: 太平興國中，有南唐軍校馬光璉等亡命荊楚，結徒為盜。

translations.literal: In the Taiping Xingguo era the Southern Tang army officer Ma Guanglian and others fled as outlaws to Jingchu and gathered a band to rob.
translations.idiomatic: During Taiping Xingguo, the former Southern Tang army officer Ma Guanglian and others fled to Jingchu as outlaws and gathered a band of robbers.

sentences.zh: 羲受詔，縛光璉以獻，太宗壯之。

translations.literal: Xi received the edict, bound Guanglian and presented him; Emperor Taizong was impressed.
translations.idiomatic: Xi received the order, bound Guanglian, and presented him to court; Emperor Taizong was greatly pleased.

sentences.zh: 積勞改西頭供奉官，決獄於淮南諸州。

translations.literal: For accumulated service he was changed to western palace attendant officer and adjudicated cases in the prefectures of Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: For long service he was promoted to western palace attendant officer and sent to adjudicate cases in the Huainan prefectures.

sentences.zh: 淳化中，又督洛南采銅。

translations.literal: In the Chunhua era he again supervised copper mining at Luonan.
translations.idiomatic: During Chunhua he was again put in charge of copper mining at Luonan.

sentences.zh: 雷有終稱其有心計，遣監興國軍茶務。

translations.literal: Lei Youzhong praised him for having resourceful plans and sent him to supervise the tea monopoly at Xingguo Army.
translations.idiomatic: Lei Youzhong praised him for his shrewdness and dispatched him to supervise tea affairs at Xingguo Army.

sentences.zh: 會楊允恭改茶鹽法，薦羲掌真州榷務，尋提點淮南西路茶鹽，得羨餘十餘萬，遂與允恭同為江、淮製置，擢授閣門祗候，兼製置礬稅。

translations.literal: When Yang Yungong reformed the tea and salt laws, he recommended Xi to manage the Zhenzhou monopoly office; soon afterward Xi was appointed tea and salt intendant for western Huainan Circuit, yielding a surplus of more than one hundred thousand, and then he and Yungong together served as Jiang-Huai commissioners; he was promoted to door attendant and also made commissioner for alum tax.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Yungong reformed the tea and salt laws, he recommended Xi to run the monopoly office at Zhenzhou. Xi was soon appointed intendant of tea and salt for western Huainan Circuit, where he produced a surplus of more than one hundred thousand; he and Yungong then served together as Jiang-Huai commissioners. Xi was promoted to door attendant and also made commissioner for alum tax.

sentences.zh: 咸平初，入奏，真宗麵加慰勞。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xianping he entered court to report; Emperor Zhenzong personally added words of comfort and praise.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Xianping reign he came to court to report, and Emperor Zhenzong personally comforted and praised him.

sentences.zh: 淮南榷鹽，二歲增錢八十三萬餘貫，以勞改內殿崇班，又兼製置荊湖路。

translations.literal: In Huainan salt monopoly, over two years revenue increased by more than eight hundred thirty thousand strings of cash; for this merit he was changed to Inner Hall Honored Rank, and also concurrently made commissioner of Jinghu Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Under his salt monopoly in Huainan, revenue rose by more than eight hundred thirty thousand strings of cash in two years. For this service he was promoted to Inner Hall Honored Rank and also made commissioner of Jinghu Circuit.

sentences.zh: 江南群盜久為民患，羲討捕皆盡。

translations.literal: Bandits in Jiangnan had long been a plague on the people; Xi hunted them down until all were eliminated.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits in Jiangnan had long plagued the people, but Xi hunted them down until none remained.

sentences.zh: 四年，領發運使事，改供備庫副使，獻議增榷酤歲十八萬緡，所增既多，尤為刻下。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he took charge of transport commissioner duties and was changed to vice commissioner of the Supply Repository; he submitted a proposal to increase the wine monopoly by one hundred eighty thousand strings per year—the increase being so large, he was especially harsh toward those below.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he assumed the duties of transport commissioner and was promoted to vice commissioner of the Supply Repository. He proposed raising the wine monopoly by one hundred eighty thousand strings a year; because the increase was so steep, he was especially harsh toward those beneath him.

sentences.zh: 會歲旱，詔罷之。

translations.literal: When drought struck that year, an edict abolished it.
translations.idiomatic: When drought struck that year, an edict abolished the increase.

sentences.zh: 景德初，遷供備庫使、知江陵府。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jingde he was transferred to Supply Repository commissioner and prefect of Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Jingde reign he was transferred to Supply Repository commissioner and appointed prefect of Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 坐舉官不如狀，削秩。

translations.literal: He was punished because a man he had recommended proved unqualified, and his rank was reduced.
translations.idiomatic: Because a man he had recommended proved unqualified, he was demoted.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符初，起授供備庫副使、宿州監軍，稍遷東染院副使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Dazhong Xiangfu he was recalled and appointed vice Supply Repository commissioner and military supervisor at Suzhou; he was gradually promoted to vice commissioner of the Eastern Dyeing Office.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Dazhong Xiangfu he was recalled and appointed vice commissioner of the Supply Repository and military supervisor at Suzhou, then gradually promoted to vice commissioner of the Eastern Dyeing Office.

sentences.zh: 明年，廣州言澄海兵嘗捕宜賊，頗希恩桀驁，軍中不能制，部送闕下。

translations.literal: The next year Guangzhou reported that Chenghai troops who had once captured Yai bandits had grown arrogant in expectation of reward and were unmanageable within the army; they were sent under escort to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Guangzhou reported that Chenghai troops who had once captured Yizhou bandits had grown arrogant in expectation of reward and could no longer be controlled in camp, so they were escorted to the capital.

sentences.zh: 上以遠方大鎮，宜得材幹之臣鎮撫之。

translations.literal: The emperor held that so great a post in a distant region ought to have a capable minister to pacify and govern it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor felt that so important a post in a distant region required a capable minister to pacify and govern it.

sentences.zh: 宰相曆言數人，皆不稱旨。

translations.literal: The chief ministers in succession named several men, but none met the emperor's wish.
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers in turn recommended several men, but none satisfied the emperor.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「秦羲可當此任。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Qin Xi can fill this post."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Qin Xi can fill this post."

sentences.zh: 復授供備庫使，充廣州鈐轄。

translations.literal: Xi was again appointed Supply Repository commissioner and made commandant of Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xi was again appointed Supply Repository commissioner and made commandant of Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 曆東染院使、知蘇州，改崇儀使、提舉在京諸司庫務。

translations.literal: He successively served as commissioner of the Eastern Dyeing Office and prefect of Suzhou, then was changed to Honored Ceremonial commissioner and put in charge of all warehouse offices in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He served successively as commissioner of the Eastern Dyeing Office and prefect of Suzhou, then was promoted to Honored Ceremonial commissioner and put in charge of all warehouse offices in the capital.

sentences.zh: 因對，求典藩郡，遷內園使、知泉州。

translations.literal: On an audience he requested appointment to a frontier prefecture and was transferred to Inner Garden commissioner and prefect of Quanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At an audience he asked to govern a frontier prefecture and was transferred to Inner Garden commissioner and prefect of Quanzhou.

sentences.zh: 天禧四年，代還。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Tianxi he completed his term and returned.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Tianxi he completed his term and returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 道病卒，年六十四。

translations.literal: He fell ill on the road and died, aged sixty-four.
translations.idiomatic: He fell ill on the road and died at the age of sixty-four.

sentences.zh: 羲知書，好為詩，喜賓客，頗有士風。
