translations.literal: Xi was literate, fond of writing poetry, enjoyed entertaining guests, and had something of a scholar's air.
translations.idiomatic: Xi was literate, fond of poetry, enjoyed entertaining guests, and had something of a scholar's bearing.

sentences.zh: 曆財貨之任，凡十餘年，精勤練習，號為稱職。

translations.literal: He held fiscal posts for more than ten years altogether, diligent and practiced, and was regarded as well qualified.
translations.idiomatic: He held fiscal posts for more than ten years in all, working diligently and skillfully, and was regarded as thoroughly competent.

sentences.zh: 謝德權

translations.literal: Xie Dequan
translations.idiomatic: Xie Dequan

sentences.zh: 謝德權，字士衡，福州人。

translations.literal: Xie Dequan, styled Shiheng, was a man of Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Dequan, styled Shiheng, was from Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 父文節，初仕王氏，為侯官令。

translations.literal: His father Wenjie at first served the Wang regime as magistrate of Houguan.
translations.idiomatic: His father Wenjie first served the Wang regime as magistrate of Houguan.

sentences.zh: 後入南唐，為忠烈都虞侯、饒州團練使，以驍勇聞。

translations.literal: Later he entered Southern Tang service as deputy commander of the Zhonglie Guard and regimental commissioner of Raozhou, famed for fierce courage.
translations.idiomatic: Later he entered Southern Tang service as deputy commander of the Zhonglie Guard and regimental commissioner of Raozhou, famed for his fierce courage.

sentences.zh: 周世宗南征，文節獨擐甲度大江，潛覘敵壘，吳人號為「鐵龍」。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizong of Zhou marched south, Wenjie alone donned armor, crossed the great river, and secretly reconnoitered the enemy camps; the Wu people called him "Iron Dragon."
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizong of Zhou marched south, Wenjie alone donned armor, crossed the great river, and secretly reconnoitered the enemy camps; the Wu people called him "Iron Dragon."

sentences.zh: 後守鄂州，拒宋師，戰沒。

translations.literal: Later he defended Ezhou, resisted Song forces, and died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Later he defended Ezhou, resisted the Song army, and died in battle.

sentences.zh: 德權初以父死事，李煜署莊宅副使。

translations.literal: Dequan at first, because his father died in service, was given the post of deputy estate commissioner by Li Yu.
translations.idiomatic: At first, because his father had died in service, Li Yu appointed Dequan deputy estate commissioner.

sentences.zh: 歸宋，詣登聞檢院自薦，補殿前承旨，遷殿直、陝西巡檢，以勞就改右侍禁。

translations.literal: After submitting to Song he went to the Petition Inspection Court to recommend himself, was appointed a palace attendant aide, was transferred to palace guard and Shaanxi circuit inspector, and for meritorious service was changed to right palace guard.
translations.idiomatic: After submitting to the Song he went to the Petition Inspection Court to recommend himself, was appointed a palace attendant aide, then transferred to palace guard and Shaanxi circuit inspector; for meritorious service he was promoted to right palace guard.

sentences.zh: 咸陽浮橋壞，轉運使宋太初命德權規畫，乃築土實岸，聚石為倉，用河中鐵牛之制，纜以竹索，繇是無患。

translations.literal: When the Xianyang floating bridge collapsed, transport commissioner Song Taichu ordered Dequan to plan the repair; he piled earth to fill the banks, gathered stones into stores, used the iron-ox system of the Yellow River, moored with bamboo cables, and thereafter there was no trouble.
translations.idiomatic: When the Xianyang floating bridge collapsed, transport commissioner Song Taichu ordered Dequan to plan the repair. He piled earth to fill the banks, gathered stones into stores, used the iron-ox mooring system of the Yellow River, and secured the bridge with bamboo cables; thereafter there was no further trouble.

sentences.zh: 咸平二年，宜州溪蠻叛，命陳堯叟往經度之，德權預其行，以單騎入蠻境，諭以朝旨，眾咸聽命。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xianping the Yizhou stream tribes rebelled; Chen Yaosou was ordered to oversee the matter; Dequan joined the mission, entered the tribal territory alone on horseback, expounded the court's will, and all obeyed.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Xianping the Yizhou stream tribes rebelled, and Chen Yaosou was ordered to oversee the matter. Dequan joined the mission, rode alone into tribal territory, expounded the court's will, and all submitted.

sentences.zh: 堯叟以聞，加閣門祗候，廣、韶、英、雄、連、賀六州都巡檢使。

translations.literal: Yaosou reported this; Dequan was promoted to door attendant and made overall circuit inspector of the six prefectures of Guang, Shao, Ying, Xiong, Lian, and He.
translations.idiomatic: Yaosou reported this, and Dequan was promoted to door attendant and made overall circuit inspector of Guang, Shao, Ying, Xiong, Lian, and He prefectures.

sentences.zh: 代歸，提點京城倉草場。

translations.literal: When his term ended and he returned, he was appointed intendant of the capital's granaries and hay fields.
translations.idiomatic: When his term ended and he returned, he was appointed intendant of the capital's granaries and hay fields.

sentences.zh: 先是，廥積多患地下濕，德權累甓為台以藉之，遂無敗腐。

translations.literal: Previously stored grain often suffered from dampness below; Dequan stacked bricks into platforms beneath it, and spoilage ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Previously stored grain often spoiled from dampness below ground; Dequan stacked bricks into platforms to support it, and spoilage ceased.

sentences.zh: 京城衢巷狹隘，命德權廣之。

translations.literal: The capital's lanes and alleys were narrow and cramped; Dequan was ordered to widen them.
translations.idiomatic: The capital's lanes and alleys were narrow and cramped, and Dequan was ordered to widen them.

sentences.zh: 既受詔，則先撤貴要邸舍，群議紛然。

translations.literal: Once he had received the edict he first demolished the mansions of the powerful; public outcry was vehement.
translations.idiomatic: Once he received the edict he first demolished the mansions of the powerful, and public outcry was vehement.

sentences.zh: 有詔止之，德權麵請曰：「臣己受命，不可中止。

translations.literal: An edict was issued to stop him; Dequan personally petitioned: "Your servant has already received the commission—it cannot be halted.
translations.idiomatic: An edict was issued to stop him, but Dequan personally petitioned, "Your servant has already received the commission—it cannot be halted.

sentences.zh: 今沮事者皆權豪輩，吝屋室僦資耳，非有他也。」

translations.literal: Those who now obstruct the work are all powerful magnates, begrudging only the rent on their houses—there is nothing else to it."
translations.idiomatic: Those who now obstruct the work are all powerful magnates begrudging only the rent on their houses—there is nothing else to it."

sentences.zh: 上從之。

translations.literal: The emperor agreed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 因條上衢巷廣袤及禁鼓昏曉之制。

translations.literal: He then submitted detailed regulations on the breadth of lanes and alleys and the curfew-bell system for dusk and dawn.
translations.idiomatic: He then submitted detailed regulations on the width of lanes and alleys and the curfew-bell system for dusk and dawn.

sentences.zh: 會有凶人劉曄、僧澄雅訟執政與許州民陰構西夏為叛者，詔溫仲舒、謝泌鞫問，令德權監之。

translations.literal: Meanwhile the malefactor Liu Ye and the monk Chengya sued, alleging that chief ministers and a Xuzhou commoner had secretly colluded with Western Xia in rebellion; Wen Zhongshu and Xie Bi were ordered to examine the case, with Dequan supervising.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile the malefactor Liu Ye and the monk Chengya brought suit, alleging that chief ministers and a commoner of Xuzhou had secretly colluded with Western Xia in rebellion; Wen Zhongshu and Xie Bi were ordered to examine the case, with Dequan supervising.

sentences.zh: 既而按驗無狀，翌日，對便殿，具奏其妄。

translations.literal: Investigation then found no substance to the charges; the next day, at audience in the informal hall, they fully reported its falsity.
translations.idiomatic: Investigation then found no substance to the charges; the next day, at audience in the informal hall, they fully reported that the accusation was false.

sentences.zh: 泌獨曰：「 追攝大臣，獄狀乃具。」

translations.literal: Bi alone said: "If we summon and detain great ministers, the case record will then be complete."
translations.idiomatic: Bi alone said, "If we summon and detain great ministers, the case record will then be complete."

sentences.zh: 德權曰：「泌欲陷大臣耶！

translations.literal: Dequan said: "Does Bi wish to trap great ministers!
translations.idiomatic: Dequan said, "Does Bi wish to trap great ministers!

sentences.zh: 若使大臣無罪受辱，則人君何以使臣，臣下何以事君？」

translations.literal: If great ministers suffer disgrace though innocent, how can the ruler employ ministers, and how can ministers serve the ruler?"
translations.idiomatic: If great ministers suffer disgrace though innocent, how can the ruler employ ministers, and how can ministers serve the ruler?"

sentences.zh: 仲舒曰：「德權所奏甚善。」

translations.literal: Zhongshu said: "What Dequan has stated is very good."
translations.idiomatic: Zhongshu said, "What Dequan has stated is very good."

sentences.zh: 上乃可之。

translations.literal: The emperor then approved it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then approved it.

sentences.zh: 六年，命城新樂縣，遷供奉官。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was ordered to fortify Xinle County and was transferred to palace attendant officer.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was ordered to fortify Xinle County and was promoted to palace attendant officer.

sentences.zh: 又命浚北平砦濠，葺蒲陰城。

translations.literal: He was also ordered to dredge the moat at Beiping Fort and repair Puyin city.
translations.idiomatic: He was also ordered to dredge the moat at Beiping Fort and repair Puyin city.

sentences.zh: 一日，遽乘傳詣闕求對，且言：「邊民多挈族入城居止。

translations.literal: One day he suddenly took post-horses to the capital seeking audience, and said: "Frontier people have largely brought their clans into the cities to live.
translations.idiomatic: One day he suddenly rode post-horses to the capital seeking an audience and said, "Frontier people have largely brought their clans into the cities to live.

sentences.zh: 前歲契丹入塞，傅潛閉壘自固，康保裔被擒，王師未有勝捷。

translations.literal: The year before last when the Khitan entered the passes, Fu Qian closed his fort and held fast, Kang Baoyi was captured, and the imperial army had no victory to report.
translations.idiomatic: The year before last, when the Khitan entered the passes, Fu Qian closed his fort and held fast, Kang Baoyi was captured, and the imperial army had no victory to report.

sentences.zh: 臣以為今歲契丹必寇內地，令邊兵聚屯一處，尤非便利，願速分戍鎮、定、高陽三路。

translations.literal: Your servant believes that this year the Khitan will surely raid the interior; to mass frontier troops in one place is especially ill-advised—I beg that garrisons be quickly divided among the three routes of Zhen, Ding, and Gaoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant believes that this year the Khitan will surely raid the interior. Massing frontier troops in one place is especially ill-advised—I beg that garrisons be quickly divided among the three routes of Zhen, Ding, and Gaoyang.

sentences.zh: 天雄城壘闊遠，請急詔蹙之，仍葺澶州城，北治德清軍城塹，以為豫備。

translations.literal: The Tianxiong fortifications are vast and spread out—please urgently order them tightened; still repair Chenzhou city, and fortify the walls and moat of Deqing Army to the north as a reserve measure.
translations.idiomatic: The Tianxiong fortifications are vast and spread out—please urgently order them tightened. Repair Chenzhou city as well, and fortify the walls and moat of Deqing Army to the north as a reserve measure.

sentences.zh: 臣實慮蒲陰工作未訖，寇必暴至。」

translations.literal: Your servant truly fears that work at Puyin is not yet finished and the enemy will suddenly arrive."
translations.idiomatic: Your servant truly fears that work at Puyin is not yet finished and the enemy will suddenly arrive."

sentences.zh: 上慰遣之，既而契丹果圍蒲陰。

translations.literal: The emperor comforted and sent him off; soon afterward the Khitan indeed besieged Puyin.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor comforted and sent him off; soon afterward the Khitan indeed besieged Puyin.

sentences.zh: 及聞有詔修河北行宮，德權又驛奏，請車駕毋渡河，及至澶州，德權單馬間道赴行在。

translations.literal: When word came of an edict to build traveling palaces in Hebei, Dequan again memorialized by post relay, begging the imperial carriage not to cross the river; when the court reached Chenzhou, Dequan came alone by horse through a bypath to the emperor's encampment.
translations.idiomatic: When word came of an edict to build traveling palaces in Hebei, Dequan again memorialized by post relay, begging the imperial carriage not to cross the river. When the court reached Chenzhou, Dequan came alone on horseback by a bypath to the emperor's encampment.

sentences.zh: 未幾，遷內殿崇班、提轄三司衙司。

translations.literal: Before long he was transferred to Inner Hall Honored Rank and put in charge of the Three Departments' clerical offices.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was promoted to Inner Hall Honored Rank and put in charge of the Three Departments' clerical offices.

sentences.zh: 德權為設條製，均其差使。

translations.literal: Dequan established regulations to balance their assignments of duty.
translations.idiomatic: Dequan established regulations to balance their assignments of duty.

sentences.zh: 有大將隸內侍主藏，內侍為奏留，規免煩重之役。

translations.literal: A general officer subordinate to an inner-attendant treasury custodian had the attendant memorialize to keep him, scheming to evade heavy and troublesome duties.
translations.idiomatic: A general officer subordinate to an inner-attendant treasury custodian had the attendant memorialize to keep him on staff, scheming to evade heavy and troublesome duties.

sentences.zh: 德權攜奏白上，極言僥幸，上稱其有守。

translations.literal: Dequan brought the memorial directly to the emperor, speaking sternly against such favoritism; the emperor praised his integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Dequan brought the memorial directly to the emperor and spoke sternly against such favoritism; the emperor praised his integrity.

sentences.zh: 又命提總京城四排岸，領護汴河兼督輦運。

translations.literal: He was again ordered to take overall charge of the capital's four river embankment offices, oversee the Bian River, and supervise transport by imperial carriage.
translations.idiomatic: He was again ordered to take overall charge of the capital's four river embankment offices, oversee the Bian River, and supervise transport by imperial carriage.

sentences.zh: 前是，歲役浚河夫三十萬，而主者因循，堤防不固，但挑沙擁岸址，或河流泛濫，即中流復填淤矣。

translations.literal: Previously, three hundred thousand laborers were levied each year to dredge the river, but those in charge were lax, the dikes were not secure—they merely scraped sand to pile at the bank base—and when the river flooded, the middle channel would silt up again.
translations.idiomatic: Previously three hundred thousand laborers were levied each year to dredge the river, but those in charge were lax and the dikes were not secure—they merely scraped sand to pile at the bank base—and when the river flooded, the middle channel would silt up again.

sentences.zh: 德權須以沙盡至土為垠，棄沙堤外，遣三班使者分地以主其役。

translations.literal: Dequan required dredging until sand gave way to earth as the margin, cast sand outside the dike, and sent third-rank envoys to divide the territory and supervise the work.
translations.idiomatic: Dequan required dredging until sand gave way to earth as the margin, cast sand outside the dike, and sent third-rank envoys to divide the territory and supervise the work.

sentences.zh: 又為大錐以試築堤之虛實，或引錐可入者，即坐所轄官吏，多被譴免者。

translations.literal: He also devised a large auger to test the solidity of the dikes; where the auger could be driven in, the responsible officials were punished, and many were dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: He also devised a large auger to test the solidity of the dikes; wherever the auger could be driven in, the responsible officials were punished, and many were dismissed.

sentences.zh: 植樹數十萬以固岸。

translations.literal: He planted several hundred thousand trees to strengthen the banks.
translations.idiomatic: He planted several hundred thousand trees to strengthen the banks.

sentences.zh: 建議廢京師鑄錢監，徙西窯務於河陰，大省勞費。

translations.literal: He proposed abolishing the capital mint and moving the western furnace office to Heyin, greatly saving labor and expense.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed abolishing the capital mint and moving the western furnace office to Heyin, greatly saving labor and expense.

sentences.zh: 改崇儀副使，兼領東西八作司。

translations.literal: He was changed to vice Honored Ceremonial commissioner and concurrently directed the eastern and western construction offices.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice Honored Ceremonial commissioner and concurrently directed the eastern and western construction offices.

sentences.zh: 先時，每營造患工少，至終歲不成。

translations.literal: Previously every construction project suffered from too few workers and might remain unfinished by year's end.
translations.idiomatic: Previously every construction project suffered from too few workers and might remain unfinished by year's end.

sentences.zh: 德權按其役，皆克日而就。

translations.literal: Dequan monitored the work, and all projects were completed on schedule.
translations.idiomatic: Dequan monitored the work, and all projects were completed on schedule.

sentences.zh: 德權清苦幹事，好興功利，多所經畫。

translations.literal: Dequan was austere and hardworking, fond of promoting useful projects, and planned many undertakings.
translations.idiomatic: Dequan was austere and hardworking, fond of promoting useful projects, and planned many undertakings.

sentences.zh: 見官吏徇私者，必麵斥之，所至整肅。

translations.literal: When he saw officials acting from private interest he would rebuke them to their faces; wherever he went, order was restored.
translations.idiomatic: When he saw officials acting from private interest he would rebuke them to their faces; wherever he went, order was restored.

sentences.zh: 然喜采察纖微，以聞於上，朝論惡之。

translations.literal: Yet he liked to investigate minute matters and report them to the throne, and court opinion despised this.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he liked to investigate minute matters and report them to the throne, and court opinion despised this.

sentences.zh: 閻日新

translations.literal: Yan Rixin
translations.idiomatic: Yan Rixin

sentences.zh: 閻日新，宿州臨渙人。

translations.literal: Yan Rixin was a native of Linhuan in Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Rixin was a native of Linhuan in Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 少為本州牙職，補三司使役吏。

translations.literal: In youth he served as a local adjutant clerk and was appointed a clerk in the Three Departments commissioner's office.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he served as a local adjutant clerk and was appointed a clerk in the Three Departments commissioner's office.

sentences.zh: 淳化中，選隸壽王府，主邸中記簿。

translations.literal: During Chunhua he was selected to serve the Prince of Shou's household and kept its registry accounts.
translations.idiomatic: During Chunhua he was selected to serve the Prince of Shou's household and kept its registry accounts.

sentences.zh: 真宗即位，擢為供奉官，提點雄、霸、靜戎軍榷場。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhenzong acceded he was promoted to palace attendant officer and made intendant of the monopoly markets at Xiong, Ba, and Jingrong Army.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhenzong acceded he was promoted to palace attendant officer and made intendant of the monopoly markets at Xiong, Ba, and Jingrong Army.

sentences.zh: 咸平元年，遷內殿崇班、永興軍駐泊都監，徙劍門關兼知劍門縣，就加供備庫副使、慶州都監。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xianping he was transferred to Inner Hall Honored Rank and overall supervisor of Yongxing Army garrison troops, moved to Jianmen Pass while also serving as magistrate of Jianmen County, and concurrently promoted to vice Supply Repository commissioner and military supervisor of Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xianping he was promoted to Inner Hall Honored Rank and overall supervisor of Yongxing Army garrison troops, transferred to Jianmen Pass while also serving as magistrate of Jianmen County, and concurrently promoted to vice Supply Repository commissioner and military supervisor of Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 景德初，命管勾邠、寧、環州駐泊兵馬。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jingde he was ordered to manage the garrison troops at Bin, Ning, and Huan prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Jingde reign he was ordered to manage the garrison troops at Bin, Ning, and Huan prefectures.

sentences.zh: 時，部署張凝屢入邊界焚族帳，日新皆提兵應援。

translations.literal: At that time the deployment commander Zhang Ning repeatedly entered the borderlands to burn tribal camps, and Rixin each time led troops to support him.
translations.idiomatic: At that time deployment commander Zhang Ning repeatedly entered the borderlands to burn tribal camps, and Rixin each time led troops to support him.

sentences.zh: 俄知涇州，未幾，移慶州。

translations.literal: Soon he was made prefect of Jingzhou; before long he was transferred to Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made prefect of Jingzhou; before long he was transferred to Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 上言：「野溪、三門等族恃嶮隘，桀黠難製，請開古川道，東至樂業鎮，西出府城。」

translations.literal: He memorialized: "The Yexi, Sanmen, and other tribes rely on rugged passes—they are crafty and hard to control; I request opening the ancient river route east to Leye garrison and west out from the prefectural city."
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized, "The Yexi, Sanmen, and other tribes rely on rugged passes—they are crafty and hard to control. I request opening the ancient river route east to Leye garrison and west out from the prefectural city."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: The request was granted.

sentences.zh: 就轉供備庫使、知環州兼邠寧環慶路鈐轄、緣邊都巡檢使、安撫都監。

translations.literal: He was then transferred to Supply Repository commissioner, prefect of Huanzhou, and concurrently commandant of Bin-Ning-Huan-Qing Circuit, overall frontier circuit inspector, and pacification supervisor.
translations.idiomatic: He was then promoted to Supply Repository commissioner and prefect of Huanzhou, and concurrently made commandant of Bin-Ning-Huan-Qing Circuit, overall frontier circuit inspector, and pacification supervisor.

sentences.zh: 俄換涇原儀渭路。

translations.literal: Soon he was reassigned to the Jingyuan-Yiwei route.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was reassigned to the Jingyuan-Yiwei route.

sentences.zh: 二年，遷如京使，領萬州刺史。

translations.literal: In the second year he was transferred to Capital Envoy and given the title of prefect of Wanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was promoted to Capital Envoy and given the title of prefect of Wanzhou.

sentences.zh: 上朝陵、東封，皆命為行宮使。

translations.literal: For imperial tomb visits and the eastern Mount Tai feng sacrifice, he was each time appointed traveling-palace commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: For imperial tomb visits and the eastern Mount Tai feng sacrifice, he was each time appointed traveling-palace commissioner.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符初，改文思使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Dazhong Xiangfu he was changed to Literary Reflection commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Dazhong Xiangfu he was promoted to Literary Reflection commissioner.

sentences.zh: 日新起胥史，好雲為以進取，嘗上言：「群臣子弟以蔭得官，往往未童齔以受奉，望自今年二十以上，乃給廩。

translations.literal: Rixin rose from clerk ranks, fond of grand proposals for advancement; he once memorialized: "Sons and younger brothers of ministers who obtain office by inherited privilege often receive salaries before they even reach childhood—I hope that from this year stipends will be granted only from age twenty upward.
translations.idiomatic: Rixin rose from clerk ranks and was fond of grand proposals for advancement. He once memorialized, "Sons and younger brothers of ministers who obtain office by inherited privilege often receive salaries before they even reach childhood—I hope that from this year stipends will be granted only from age twenty upward.

sentences.zh: 又京城百官早朝，而學士、丞、郎、舍人以上，導從嗬止太盛，難於趨避，望令裁減。」

translations.literal: Again, when all capital officials attend early court, the outriders and shouting attendants of academicians, vice-directors, bureau directors, and secretaries and above are too numerous and make it hard to pass—I hope an order will be issued to reduce them."
translations.idiomatic: Again, when all capital officials attend early court, the outriders and shouting attendants of academicians, vice-directors, bureau directors, and secretaries and above are too numerous and make it hard to pass—I hope an order will be issued to reduce them."

sentences.zh: 又屢請對，多所建白。

translations.literal: He also repeatedly sought audiences and made many proposals.
translations.idiomatic: He also repeatedly sought audiences and made many proposals.

sentences.zh: 且自陳筋力尚壯，願正授刺郡，守邊城以效用。

translations.literal: Moreover he declared himself still vigorous and asked to be formally appointed to a prefecture with a charter, to guard a frontier city and serve usefully.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover he declared himself still vigorous and asked to be formally appointed to a chartered prefecture, to guard a frontier city and serve usefully.

sentences.zh: 俄真拜坊州刺史、知渭州兼涇原路駐泊鈐轄。

translations.literal: Soon he was truly appointed prefect of Fangzhou, acting prefect of Weizhou, and commandant of Jingyuan Circuit garrison troops.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was formally appointed prefect of Fangzhou, acting prefect of Weizhou, and commandant of Jingyuan Circuit garrison troops.

sentences.zh: 將祀汾陰，故改知同州事，儼信頓即日新所部，車駕至，迎謁獻方物。

translations.literal: When the emperor was about to sacrifice at Fenyin, he was therefore changed to acting prefect of Tongzhou; Yanxindun lay in Rixin's jurisdiction, and when the imperial carriage arrived he went out to welcome him and presented local products.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor was about to sacrifice at Fenyin, he was therefore transferred to acting prefect of Tongzhou. Yanxindun lay in Rixin's jurisdiction, and when the imperial carriage arrived he went out to welcome the emperor and presented local products.

sentences.zh: 勞問久之，遂從祀睢上，賜以襲衣、金帶。

translations.literal: The emperor questioned and comforted him at length, then allowed him to follow the sacrifice at the Sui altar and bestowed on him ceremonial robes and a gold belt.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor questioned and comforted him at length, then allowed him to follow the sacrifice at the Sui altar and bestowed on him ceremonial robes and a gold belt.

sentences.zh: 還過新市鎮，又設彩樓樂伎以迎駕。

translations.literal: On the return journey through Xinshi town he again erected decorated towers and staged musicians to welcome the imperial progress.
translations.idiomatic: On the return journey through Xinshi town he again erected decorated towers and staged musicians to welcome the imperial progress.

sentences.zh: 明年，徙知徐州。

translations.literal: The next year he was transferred to prefect of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he was transferred to prefect of Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 代還，以足疾，改右領軍衛大將軍、昭州團練使、知單州。

translations.literal: When his term ended and he returned, because of foot ailment he was changed to grand general of the Right Leading Army Guard, regimental commissioner of Zhaozhou, and acting prefect of Shanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When his term ended and he returned, because of a foot ailment he was transferred to grand general of the Right Leading Army Guard, regimental commissioner of Zhaozhou, and acting prefect of Shanzhou.

sentences.zh: 疾益甚，許還京師。

translations.literal: His illness grew worse and he was permitted to return to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: His illness grew worse and he was permitted to return to the capital.

sentences.zh: 天禧初，卒，年六十八。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianxi he died, aged sixty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Tianxi reign he died at the age of sixty-eight.

sentences.zh: 靳懷德

translations.literal: Jin Huaide
translations.idiomatic: Jin Huaide

sentences.zh: 靳懷德，博州高唐人。

translations.literal: Jin Huaide was a native of Gaotang in Bozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Huaide was from Gaotang in Bo Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 祖昌範，殿中丞。

translations.literal: His grandfather Changfan was palace attendant.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Changfan served as palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 父隱，禹城令。

translations.literal: His father Yin was magistrate of Yucheng.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yin was magistrate of Yucheng.

sentences.zh: 懷德太平興國中明法，解褐廣安軍判官。

translations.literal: Huaide passed the statutes examination in the Taiping Xingguo era and on leaving his student status was made judge of Guangan Army.
translations.idiomatic: Huaide passed the statutes examination during Taiping Xingguo and on entering service was made judge of Guangan Army.

sentences.zh: 秩滿，授鴻臚寺丞，曆著作佐郎、太子左讚善大夫、通判相州，改殿中丞、通判廣州，遷國子博士、通判滄州。

translations.literal: When his term expired he was appointed vice commissioner of the Court for Diplomatic Reception, successively served as assistant editorial director, left aide to the heir apparent, and vice prefect of Xiangzhou, was changed to palace attendant and vice prefect of Guangzhou, and was transferred to Guozijian erudite and vice prefect of Cangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When his term ended he was made vice commissioner of the Court for Diplomatic Reception, then served in turn as assistant editorial director, left aide to the heir apparent, and vice prefect of Xiang Prefecture, became palace attendant and vice prefect of Guang Prefecture, and was promoted to Guozijian erudite and vice prefect of Cang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 曆虞部、比部員外郎，又通判莫州，知德州。

translations.literal: He successively served as vice director of the works and comparisons bureaus, again as vice prefect of Mozhou, and as prefect of Dezhou.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as vice director of the works and comparisons bureaus, then as vice prefect of Mo Prefecture and prefect of De Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 咸平中，契丹入寇，懷德固守城壁，又轉運使劉通言其善政，連有詔褒之。

translations.literal: In the Xianping era, when the Khitans invaded, Huaide firmly held the walls, and transport commissioner Liu Tong also reported his good governance; edicts of praise followed one after another.
translations.idiomatic: During Xianping, when the Khitans invaded, Huaide held the city walls firm, and transport commissioner Liu Tong praised his governance as well, so the court issued repeated edicts commending him.

sentences.zh: 徙知密州，會留後孔守正之鎮，代還。

translations.literal: He was transferred to govern Mizhou; when the military governor Kong Shouzheng took up his post, Huaide was relieved and returned.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Mi Prefecture, and when military governor Kong Shouzheng took up his command, Huaide was relieved and returned.

sentences.zh: 鹽鐵使陳恕、判官王濟薦其武幹，換如京使、知邛州。

translations.literal: Salt and iron commissioner Chen Shu and judge Wang Ji recommended his martial ability, and he was changed to capital envoy and made prefect of Qiongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Salt and iron commissioner Chen Shu and judge Wang Ji recommended his martial ability, and he was made capital envoy and prefect of Qiong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 懷德本名湘，素遊寇準之門，準父名湘，景德中，準方為相，懷德乃改名焉。

translations.literal: Huaide's original name was Xiang; he had long associated with Kou Zhun's household, and Zhun's father's name was also Xiang. In the Jingde era, when Zhun had just become chief minister, Huaide thereupon changed his name.
translations.idiomatic: Huaide had originally been named Xiang and long moved in Kou Zhun's circle; Zhun's father had also been named Xiang. In Jingde, when Zhun had just become chief minister, Huaide changed his name.

sentences.zh: 俄知滄州。

translations.literal: Shortly he governed Cangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He soon became prefect of Cang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符初，召還，復遣之任，吏民詣轉運使李士衡借留懷德，士衡以聞。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Dazhong Xiangfu he was summoned back, then again sent to his post; officials and people went to transport commissioner Li Shiheng to ask to retain Huaide on loan, and Shiheng reported this.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Dazhong Xiangfu he was recalled, then sent out again; local officials and people petitioned transport commissioner Li Shiheng to keep Huaide on loan, and Shiheng reported this to the throne.

sentences.zh: 未幾，遷文思使。

translations.literal: Before long he was transferred to commissioner of the Literary Atelier.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was made commissioner of the Literary Atelier.

sentences.zh: 三年秋，以江左旱歉，命為洪、虔十州安撫都監。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the third year, because of drought and famine in the lower Yangzi region, he was ordered to serve as overall pacification supervisor of the ten prefectures of Hong and Qian.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn, because of drought and famine south of the Yangzi, he was appointed overall pacification supervisor of the ten prefectures of Hong and Qian.

sentences.zh: 未至任，改知曹州。

translations.literal: Before he reached his post he was changed to govern Caozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Before he reached his post he was reassigned to Cao Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 明年春，選為益州鈐轄，加領長州刺史。

translations.literal: The next spring he was selected as commandant of Yizhou and additionally given the prefecture of Changzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The following spring he was chosen as commandant of Yi Prefecture and additionally made prefect of Chang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 懷德曆官以強幹稱，然酗酒多失，將行，別詔戒勖。

translations.literal: Huaide was known through his offices for forceful capability, yet he drank heavily and often erred; as he was about to depart, a separate edict admonished and encouraged him.
translations.idiomatic: Huaide had a reputation for forceful competence, but he drank heavily and often blundered; before he set out, a special edict admonished him.

sentences.zh: 真宗又麵諭之，就遷北作坊使。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhenzong also instructed him face to face, and he was thereupon transferred to commissioner of the northern workshops.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhenzong also instructed him in person and promptly promoted him to commissioner of the northern workshops.

sentences.zh: 在劍外，軍民甚畏愛之。

translations.literal: Beyond the Sword Pass, soldiers and civilians greatly feared and loved him.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond the Sword Pass, soldiers and civilians both feared and loved him.

sentences.zh: 復以善職入拜西上閣門使，改領昭州刺史、知澶州。

translations.literal: Again for good service he entered court as western upper Gate commissioner, was changed to hold the prefecture of Zhaozhou, and governed Danzhou.
translations.idiomatic: For good service he was again summoned to court as western upper Gate commissioner, made prefect of Zhao Prefecture, and sent to govern Chan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 是州居水陸之要，懷德悉心撫治，頗著政績，使車往復，多稱譽焉。

translations.literal: That prefecture lay at a key point of water and land routes; Huaide devoted himself to governing and comforting it and achieved considerable administrative success, and traveling commissioners going back and forth often praised him.
translations.idiomatic: That prefecture stood at a vital junction of water and land routes; Huaide governed it with devoted care and won a strong record, and touring commissioners often praised him.

sentences.zh: 又知陝州，逾年，歸闕而卒，時天禧元年，年七十三。

translations.literal: He next governed Shanzhou; after more than a year he returned to court and died, in the first year of Tianxi, aged seventy-three.
translations.idiomatic: He next governed Shan Prefecture; a year later he returned to court and died in the first year of Tianxi at the age of seventy-three.

sentences.zh: 論曰：世乏全材，則各錄其所長而用焉，亦皆可以集事功。

translations.literal: The commentary says: When the age lacks men of complete talent, each man's strengths are recorded and put to use, and all alike can assemble achievements.
translations.idiomatic: The commentators say: When the age lacks men of complete talent, each man's strengths are noted and put to use, and all can still accomplish real work.

sentences.zh: 允恭有心計，好言事，是時摘山煮海，方舟之漕，規制未備，故因其建白而從之，利甚博焉。

translations.literal: Yungong had shrewd calculation and liked to speak on affairs; at that time mountain tea and sea salt, and transport by linked boats, lacked complete regulations, so because of his proposals the court followed him, and the profit was very great.
translations.idiomatic: Yungong was shrewd and fond of policy debate; at that time the systems for mountain tea, sea salt, and barge transport were still incomplete, so the court followed his proposals, and the gains were considerable.

sentences.zh: 羲亦精心敏職，士大夫許其醞藉。

translations.literal: Xi also worked with devoted care and alert competence, and scholar-officials approved his cultured restraint.
translations.idiomatic: Xi too served with devoted care and alert competence, and the literati praised his cultured restraint.

sentences.zh: 德權清廉強忮，矯名好威，然其斥謝泌以大臣非可受辱，識堂陛之分，長者之言哉。

translations.literal: Dequan was incorruptible, forceful, and jealous, currying reputation and fond of authority; yet in rebuking Xie Mi that a great minister must not suffer insult, he recognized the distinction between hall and steps—words worthy of an elder.
translations.idiomatic: Dequan was incorruptible, forceful, and jealous, eager for reputation and fond of authority; yet in rebuking Xie Mi for saying a great minister must not be insulted, he showed he understood the difference between hall and steps—words worthy of an elder statesman.

sentences.zh: 延德而下，遘會進陟，迭居事任，其指使治跡，各有可取者焉。

translations.literal: From Yande downward, meeting opportunity they advanced in rank, successively holding posts of responsibility; in their direction and traces of governance each had something worth taking.
translations.idiomatic: From Yande on down, these men rose when opportunity came and held office in turn; each left a record of governance with something worth taking.
